question:
The following text is adapted from William Shakespeare’s 1597 play The Tragedy of King Richard III. Richard is reflecting on the recent arrest of his brother, the Duke of Clarence, on suspicion of treason against King Edward IV. Derby, Hastings, Buckingham, Rivers, Dorset, and Grey are also members of the English nobility.

RICHARD: I do the wrong, and first begin to brawl.
The secret mischiefs that I set [flowing]
I lay unto the grievous charge of others.
Clarence, whom I indeed have cast in darkness,
I do beweep to many simple [gullible people],
Namely, to Derby, Hastings, Buckingham;
And tell them ’tis the Queen and her allies
That stir the King against the Duke my brother.
Now they believe it, and withal whet me
To be revenged on Rivers, Dorset, Grey.

Which choice best describes what happens in the text?
choices: Richard attributes Clarence’s troubles to both his own secret plotting and the distrust of Clarence that the queen and her allies Derby, Hastings, and Buckingham have planted in the king’s mind.

Richard describes having wept as he informed Derby, Hastings, and Buckingham that the queen and her allies convinced the king to act against Clarence, and says that the earnestness of his grief caused them to accept his version of events.

Richard acknowledges that his mischievous nature has spurred him to commit misdeeds in the past, including instigating enmity between the king and Clarence, but he reports that he has hitherto not lost the trust of the queen and her allies.

Richard indicates that he has pretended to be aggrieved about Clarence’s situation and has proclaimed it to be the fault of the queen and her allies, but in reality, he has caused the hostility the king feels toward Clarence.
explanation:
Here’s a clear, line-by-line interpretation in modern English:

I do the wrong, and first begin to brawl.
I am the one who commits the wrongdoing and starts the conflict.

The secret mischiefs that I set flowing
The hidden schemes and trouble that I put into motion

I lay unto the grievous charge of others.
I blame those serious crimes on other people.

Clarence, whom I indeed have cast in darkness,
Clarence, whom I have truly caused to be imprisoned and ruined,

I do beweep to many simple [gullible people],
I pretend to mourn and feel sorrow in front of naïve, easily fooled people,

Namely, to Derby, Hastings, Buckingham;
Specifically, to Derby, Hastings, and Buckingham.

And tell them ’tis the Queen and her allies
And I tell them it is the queen and the people aligned with her

That stir the King against the Duke my brother.
Who have provoked the king into turning against my brother, the Duke of Clarence.

Now they believe it, and withal whet me
Now they believe this lie, and at the same time they urge and encourage me

To be revenged on Rivers, Dorset, Grey.
To take revenge on Rivers, Dorset, and Grey.

Richard is openly admitting to the audience that he himself engineered Clarence’s arrest, but he is pretending to be sad about it in public. He says he “weeps” to gullible nobles (Derby, Hastings, Buckingham) and lies, telling them that the queen and her allies are to blame. Those nobles believe him and, as a result, encourage Richard to seek revenge on the queen’s allies. In short: Richard caused the problem, then blamed others while acting innocent.

question:
Home Video Game Systems of the 1970s and 1980s

System | Manufacturer | System Type | Approximate number of units sold worldwide
ColecoVision | Coleco | console | 2,000,000
Intellivision | Mattel | console | 3,000,000
MSX | ASCII Corp | computer | 4,000,000
Game & Watch | Nintendo | handheld | 18,600,000

A student is writing a research paper on the global rise of the home video game industry during the 1970s and 1980s. The student is surprised by differences in the number of units sold by some systems compared to those sold by others. Most remarkably, the ____

Which choice most effectively uses data from the table to complete the statement?
choices: MSX sold approximately 4,000,000 units, whereas the Intellivision sold only approximately 3,000,000 units.
MSX sold approximately 18,600,000 units, whereas the Intellivision sold only approximately 2,000,000 units.
Game & Watch sold approximately 4,000,000 units, whereas the ColecoVision sold only approximately 3,000,000 units.
Game & Watch sold approximately 18,600,000 units, whereas the ColecoVision sold only approximately 2,000,000 units.
explanation:
Correct answer
Game & Watch sold approximately 18,600,000 units, whereas the ColecoVision sold only approximately 2,000,000 units.

Why this is correct
The sentence emphasizes the student’s surprise at large differences in units sold.

From the table:
• Game & Watch: 18.6 million
• ColecoVision: 2 million

Choice D highlights the largest contrast, making it the most striking and effective completion.

Why the other choices are wrong

MSX sold approximately 4,000,000 units, whereas the Intellivision sold only approximately 3,000,000 units.
• Difference is relatively small and not “most remarkable.”

MSX sold approximately 18,600,000 units…
• Incorrect data: MSX sold 4 million.

Game & Watch sold approximately 4,000,000 units…
• Incorrect figures and weaker contrast.

question:
In what is now southern Florida, the Calusa people (circa 1000–1600 CE) supported their relatively large population’s dietary needs with hydrological engineering rather than terrestrial farming methods. They constructed watercourts (gated coastal enclosures) out of shells and sediments to trap a variety of fish as waters rose and fell with tides and seasonal sea-level shifts; watercourt pools then held the fish for later consumption. Archaeologist Theresa Schober has posited an additional purpose of these enclosures, suggesting that they were intended to foster conch. She ties this hypothesis to the high value the sea snails would have had for the Calusa, both nutritionally and as a building material (conch shells are highly durable).

Which finding, if true, would most directly weaken Schober’s hypothesis?
choices: Samples of animal remains collected at Calusa sites reflect a greater diversity of marine species, particularly among sea snails, within the perimeter of watercourts than in locations known to have been devoted to the preparation and consumption of food.

Historical population-size estimates suggest that the sea snails and fish most common in the Calusa diet were plentiful in open coastal waters when the watercourts were constructed but decreased in abundance in the years immediately after construction.

Radar surveys of Calusa sites reveal watercourt dimensions suitable for sustaining fish of many local species but not conducive for maintaining the shallow environments with ample seagrasses that allow sea snails to thrive.

Sediment layers excavated from Calusa watercourt sites contain heterogeneous mixtures of scales from multiple species of fish and fragments of shells from various types of sea snails, but conch shells do not constitute the majority of the mixture in most of those layers.
explanation:
Correct answer
Radar surveys of Calusa sites reveal watercourt dimensions suitable for sustaining fish of many local species but not conducive for maintaining the shallow environments with ample seagrasses that allow sea snails to thrive.

Why this is correct
Schober’s hypothesis claims that the Calusa built watercourts partly to harvest sea snails, implying that the structures were well suited to snail habitats. A finding that the watercourts were not conducive to sea-snail-friendly environments directly undermines that purpose.

This is a classic mechanism challenge: if the structures could not support sea snails, then the hypothesis about their snail-harvesting function is weakened.

Why the other choices are wrong

Samples of animal remains reflect greater diversity of marine species among sea snails.
• This supports the idea that snails were important nutritionally.
• It strengthens, not weakens, the hypothesis.

Historical population estimates show snails decreased after construction.
• This could suggest overharvesting, not lack of purpose.
• It does not challenge the original intention of building watercourts.

Sediment layers contain mixed remains with shells not in the majority.
• Shells need not dominate sediment to be valuable as food or building material.
• This is inconclusive, not directly weakening.

question:
Observed Traits in a Population of Broadleaf Arrowhead, by Flowering Date

Trait | Day 5 | Day 10 | Day 15 | Day 20
Total number of open male and female per growth unit | 25 | 65 | 110 | 45
Estimated reproductive success rate of male flowers | 0.29 | 0.29 | 0.29 | 0.29
Proportion of male flowers | 0.45 | 0.50 | 0.48 | 0.13

The mating environment hypothesis predicts that populations of flowering plants compensate for reduced mating opportunities due to dichogamy (a plant’s expression of male and female functions at separate times) by increasing the bias of floral sex allocation during the flowering period, increasing the probability of successful cross-pollination. Researchers tested the hypothesis by examining a population of broadleaf arrowhead, a plant for which bloom onset generally takes longer for male flowers than for female flowers, during the flowering season. They concluded that the mating environment hypothesis is not well supported by their observational data.

Which choice best describes data from the table that support the researchers’ conclusion?
choices: Whereas the total number of open flowers per growth unit peaked on day 15, the proportion of male flowers experienced a peak earlier in the flowering season, on day 10.
Despite the sharp reduction in the total number of open flowers per growth unit from day 15 to 20, there was no decline in the estimated reproductive success rate of male flowers in that interval.
Sex allocations were largely evenly distributed on days 10 and 15 but were female biased on days 5 and 20.
Although sex allocations became overwhelmingly female biased by day 20, male flowers’ estimated reproductive success rate did not vary from day 5 to 20.
explanation:
First, restate the hypothesis being tested
The mating environment hypothesis predicts that when mating opportunities are reduced (because male and female functions occur at different times), plants should shift sex allocation during flowering in a way that increases successful cross-pollination.
So if the hypothesis were supported, we would expect changes in the proportion of male flowers to be associated with changes in male reproductive success.

Now look at the key data patterns in the table

Proportion of male flowers

Day 5: 0.45

Day 10: 0.50

Day 15: 0.48

Day 20: 0.13

By day 20, sex allocation becomes strongly female-biased (very low proportion of male flowers).

Estimated reproductive success rate of male flowers

Day 5: 0.29

Day 10: 0.29

Day 15: 0.29

Day 20: 0.29

Male reproductive success does not change at all, despite major changes in sex allocation.

Why this undermines the hypothesis
If shifting sex allocation were compensating for reduced mating opportunities, then changing the proportion of male flowers should affect male reproductive success. But the data show that even when male flowers become rare (day 20), their reproductive success remains unchanged. That means the allocation shift is not improving mating outcomes, which weakens the hypothesis.

Now evaluate the choices

Choice A
This only describes timing differences in peaks. It does not address reproductive success, so it does not support rejecting the hypothesis.

Choice B
This focuses on flower number versus reproductive success, not sex allocation bias. It doesn’t address the hypothesis directly.

Choice C
This incorrectly states that days 5 and 20 were female-biased. Day 5 is near even, not female-biased.

Choice D
This correctly captures the key contradiction:
Even though sex allocation becomes overwhelmingly female-biased by day 20, male reproductive success stays constant from day 5 through day 20. That directly supports the researchers’ conclusion that the hypothesis is not well supported.

Correct answer: D

Big takeaway
The strongest evidence against the mating environment hypothesis is that dramatic shifts in sex allocation do not lead to any improvement or change in male reproductive success.

question:
Although Grant Tavinor concludes that computer games are art by virtue of their forming a subcategory of fiction, and Berys Gaut similarly places them within the realm of cinema, neither approach adequately captures a central aspect of playing these games: when the player no longer attends to the narrative and is instead simply absorbed in the instrumentalities of gameplay. This is among the reasons philosopher C. Thi Nguyen contends that the work of computer game designers is in what he calls the medium of player agency, which the designer prescribes through rules and goals, and which elicits positive aesthetic experiences in the player who agrees to adopt it. Therefore, Nguyen’s position is that Tavinor’s and Gaut’s frameworks ___

Which choice most logically completes the text?
choices: are helpful starting points for studying computer games as art, even though these frameworks are overly simplistic.
are useful for analyzing the narrative aspects of computer games, even if neither attempts to address player agency.
overstate the influence of fiction and cinema on the narrative elements of computer games.
subsume computer games under other categories of media that do not address a feature of games that is integral to player enjoyment.
explanation:
Correct answer
subsumes computer games under other categories of media that do not address a feature of games that is integral to player enjoyment.

Why this is correct
Nguyen criticizes frameworks that treat games like fiction or cinema because they ignore player agency, which he argues is central to how games produce enjoyment.

Choice D directly captures this criticism: those frameworks misclassify games and fail to address an essential feature.

Why the other choices are wrong

Helpful starting points but overly simplistic.
• Nguyen explicitly argues they are inadequate, not merely simplistic.

Useful for analyzing narrative aspects.
• The criticism is broader than narrative; it concerns agency.

Overstate influence of fiction and cinema.
• This misrepresents the critique; influence is not the issue.

question:
As observed in a 2011 study by Emilio García-Robledo and Alfonso Corzo, macroalgal proliferation may have a suppressive effect on the abundance of cyanobacteria and other microphytobenthos (MPB)—chlorophyll-producing microbes inhabiting marine sediment—in part by reducing the amount of sunlight available to MPB. Examining benthic chlorophyll concentrations (a widely used proxy for MPB biomass) in mudflats in Curlew Bay and other coastal sites in Virginia, Alice F. Besterman and Michael L. Pace found that those concentrations did not negatively correlate with macroalgal proliferation. However, they noted that MPB may respond to low-light conditions by producing higher-than-normal concentrations of chlorophyll, and they thus concluded that ______.

Which choice most logically completes the text?
choices: researchers ought to account for the possibility that because MPB have the capacity to compensate for reduced sunlight availability, benthic chlorophyll concentrations may not always be a reliable indicator of MPB biomass.

although their finding was inconsistent with that of García-Robledo and Corzo, this discrepancy was not attributable to the ability of MPB to accelerate chlorophyll production to mitigate the negative impact of macroalgal accumulations.

although elevated levels of macroalgae do not always correspond to increased levels of benthic chlorophyll, there is likely a larger trend in MPB biomass that is related to macroalgal presence but unrelated to light conditions.

the effect of macroalgal concentrations on MPB abundance that García-Robledo and Corzo reported was not observed in Curlew Bay and other Virginia sites because low-light conditions likely are not generalizable across the sites in the studies.
explanation:
Correct answer
researchers ought to account for the possibility that because MPB have the capacity to compensate for reduced sunlight availability, benthic chlorophyll concentrations may not always be a reliable indicator of MPB biomass.

Why this is correct
The researchers observe that MPB can produce extra chlorophyll under low-light conditions, meaning chlorophyll levels may not directly reflect biomass.

This is a measurement-validity conclusion: the indicator may be misleading under certain conditions.

Why the other choices are wrong

Discrepancy not attributable to MPB ability.
• Contradicts the passage’s explicit explanation.

Larger trend unrelated to light.
• Unsupported generalization.

Low-light conditions not generalizable.
• The issue is measurement reliability, not site generalization.

question:
Neuroscientist Artin Arshamian and his team sought to determine what affects a person’s perception of an odor as pleasant: is it culture, personal taste, or aspects of human anatomy? The team assessed odor preferences in ten groups of people with different modes of living (urban, agricultural, and hunter-gatherer) including the Maniq people from a small community in Thailand and the Seri people from a small community in Mexico. The team observed that across cultures, people generally rated odors about the same: ethyl butyrate, which smells like peaches, was typically rated more pleasant than diethyl disulfide, which smells like garlic. The team’s study thus undermined the idea that ______.

Which choice most logically completes the text?
choices: a person who perceives certain odors as pleasant will likely perceive the odors as roughly equal in pleasantness.
culture significantly influences whether a person perceives an odor as pleasant or unpleasant.
personal taste has little influence on whether odors are perceived as pleasant or unpleasant.
people agree in their perception of odors as pleasant or unpleasant regardless of where they live.
explanation:
Correct answer
culture significantly influences whether a person perceives an odor as pleasant or unpleasant.

Why this is correct
The study found cross-cultural agreement on odor pleasantness, which undermines the idea that odor perception is primarily shaped by personal taste or cultural background.

Thus, the conclusion is that culture does not strongly determine pleasantness judgments—making choice B the claim that is undermined.

Why the other choices are wrong

People perceive odors as equally pleasant.
• Too absolute and not stated.

Personal taste has little influence.
• The study addresses culture, not individual taste.

People agree regardless of location.
• Overgeneralizes beyond the study’s scope.

question:
Many studies have found a positive association between levels of dissolved organic carbon and mercury in bodies of fresh water undisturbed by human activity. But Stéphane Guédron, Delphine Tisserand, and colleagues did not find this correlation in an examination of freshwater bodies impacted by wastewater. However, Ida Tjermjen and colleagues carried out a study on freshwater bodies disturbed by urban development that showed similar results to the studies on undisturbed waters, suggesting that ______.

Which choice most logically completes the text?
choices: levels of dissolved organic carbon and mercury are both much higher in bodies of fresh water impacted by wastewater than in bodies of fresh water disturbed by urban development.
Guédron, Tisserand, and colleagues’ study used different methods to measure the concentration of mercury in fresh water than Tjerngren and colleagues’ study did.
the effects of wastewater on the association between levels of dissolved organic carbon and mercury should not be taken as indicative of the effects of every type of human disturbance.
disturbances linked to wastewater affect significantly more bodies of fresh water than disturbances linked to urban development do.
explanation:
Correct answer
the effects of wastewater on the association between levels of dissolved organic carbon and mercury should not be taken as indicative of the effects of every type of human disturbance.

Why this is correct
The passage shows that different disturbances produce different results:
• Wastewater-impacted waters: no correlation
• Urban development: correlation persists

Thus, conclusions drawn from one disturbance type should not be generalized to all.

Why the other choices are wrong

Levels are higher in wastewater-impacted waters.
• Not stated.

Different measurement methods.
• No evidence of methodological differences.

Wastewater affects more bodies of water.
• Irrelevant to the logic of the conclusion.

question:
Branching in Jurisprudential Schools is one of the hundreds of thousands of manuscripts that have survived from roughly the sixteenth century to the present ______ being passed down through private libraries in the city of Timbuktu, Mali. Many of these manuscripts can be found at the Al-Wangari Manuscript Library.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

The terms included in Barry Lopez and Debra Gwartney’s Home Ground: A Guide to the American ______ such as “karst,” which refers to limestone terrain riddled with caves or sinkholes—illustrate the rich vocabulary used to describe the landforms of North America.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

Following the formation of the European Union (EU) that same year, the organizers of the 1992 Tour de France wanted the bike race to reflect the cross-national flow of people and trade that the EU had made possible. The resulting course was 2,500 miles long ______ seven separate borders of neighboring countries, modeled a vision of the EU’s unifying aims.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

As part of his I GOT UP series, Japanese conceptual artist On Kawara spent over a decade— with near daily consistency—mailing postcards to friends declaring what time he got up each day, resulting in pieces such as I Got Up at 7:19 A.M., June 6 1977. Such meticulous documentation of mundane ______ artworks that “resonate with existential, psychological and scientific implications about the time-space continuum,” according to the New York Times, became Kawara’s life’s work.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

For her film I Am Somebody (1970), a documentary about a successful months-long strike held by Black female hospital workers in Charleston, South Carolina, director Madeline Anderson chose a narrator who had participated in the ______ by allowing the narrative to be shaped by one of their own, amplified the agency and power the workers possessed.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

At a time when many women writers used male pseudonyms to gain greater freedom of self-expression by evading gender conventions, Katherine Bradley and Edith Cooper adapted the practice by publishing poetry, prose, and drama for four decades under the shared name Michael Field. ______ the duo was able to express the joint creative vision that sustained their long personal and professional partnership.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
explanation:
Correct answer
In this way,

Why this is correct
The sentence explains how Bradley and Cooper’s decision to publish under a shared name functioned: it enabled them to express a joint creative vision that sustained their partnership.

“In this way” correctly signals:
• cause → effect
• method → result

They adopted a practice, and as a result, they were able to express a shared vision.

Why the other choices are wrong

For instance,
• Introduces an example.
• No general claim is being illustrated.

Later,
• Indicates time progression.
• The sentence is explanatory, not chronological.

On the other hand,
• Signals contrast.
• No opposing idea is introduced.

question:
In a 2005 study by Mellado et al., the researchers’ aim was to analyze the diet composition of cattle in Coahuila, Mexico. ______ they aimed to analyze the ratio of three different plant subtypes within these animals’ diet: graminoids, forbs, and browse.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
explanation:
Correct answer
Specifically,

Why this is correct
The first clause states the general aim of the study (to analyze diet composition).
The second clause narrows that aim to exactly what was analyzed (the ratio of three plant subtypes).

“Specifically” correctly signals a move from general to detailed information.

Why the other choices are wrong

Instead,
• Signals replacement or opposition.
• No contrast exists.

All the same,
• Signals concession.
• No tension or contradiction exists.

Therefore,
• Signals a conclusion.
• The sentence provides clarification, not inference.

question:
John Quincy Adams employed the pseudonym “Marcellus”—a reference to a leader of an ancient Roman army—in political essays he wrote in 1793, a choice that accomplished far more than simply concealing his authorship. ______ it wasn’t an arbitrary pen name but rather a complex rhetorical strategy through which Adams aligned his political views with the venerated republican ideals of the ancient world, thereby bolstering the authority of his writing.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
explanation:
Correct answer
Indeed,

Why this is correct
The sentence explains that Adams’s pseudonym was not arbitrary, and the following clause reinforces that claim by explaining its symbolic significance.

“Indeed” works as an emphasis and confirmation marker, strengthening the preceding idea.

Why the other choices are wrong

Conversely,
• Signals contrast.
• The ideas align, not oppose.

In addition,
• Signals simple addition.
• The relationship is explanatory emphasis, not mere addition.

However,
• Signals contradiction.
• No contradiction exists.

question:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Kale is a vegetable that contains ascorbic acid, an essential nutrient for humans.
• Apricots are fruits that contain ascorbic acid.
• There is 120 milligrams (mg) of ascorbic acid per every 100 grams (g) of kale.
• There is 10 mg of ascorbic acid per every 100 g of apricot.
• Humans cannot make ascorbic acid in their bodies, so they must get it from foods, including fruits and vegetables.
• Ascorbic acid is also known as vitamin C.

The student wants to refute a claim that apricots are a better source of vitamin C than kale is. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
choices: Kale contains vitamin C (also known as ascorbic acid); in fact, there is 120 mg of vitamin C in every 100 g of kale.
Kale contains ascorbic acid (also known as vitamin C), and apricots do too.
Humans cannot make ascorbic acid in their bodies, but they can get it from kale and apricots.
With 120 mg of vitamin C per every 100 g, kale is actually a better source of vitamin C than apricots, which contain only 10 mg per every 100 g.
explanation:
Correct answer
With 120 mg of vitamin C per every 100 g, kale is actually a better source of vitamin C than apricots, which contain only 10 mg per every 100 g.

Why this is correct
The goal is to refute the claim that apricots are a better source of vitamin C than kale.

This choice:
• Directly compares both foods
• Uses precise numerical evidence
• Clearly shows kale has much more vitamin C

It is the strongest rebuttal.

Why the other choices are wrong

Kale contains vitamin C…
• States a fact but does not refute the comparison.

Kale contains ascorbic acid, and apricots do too.
• Emphasizes similarity, not superiority.

Humans cannot make ascorbic acid…
• Irrelevant to which food is the better source.

question:
• Snow hydrologist Julie Koeberle helps maintain automated snow measurement stations.
• They are called SNOTEL sites.
• There are around 90 stations throughout Wyoming.
• One is at Bear Trap Meadow.
• The data collected can help researchers make downstream water supply predictions.

Which choice most effectively uses information from the given sentences to provide an example of a SNOTEL site?
choices: The data collected by SNOTEL sites can help researchers predict downstream water supplies.
The SNOTEL site at Bear Trap Meadow is one of around 90 automated snow measurement stations in Wyoming.
Snow hydrologist Julie Koeberle helps maintain automated snow monitoring stations known as SNOTEL sites.
Located throughout Wyoming, SNOTEL sites monitor snow conditions.
explanation:
Correct answer
The SNOTEL site at Bear Trap Meadow is one of around 90 automated snow measurement stations in Wyoming.

Why this is correct
The question asks for a specific example of a SNOTEL site.

This choice:
• Names a concrete location (Bear Trap Meadow)
• Identifies it explicitly as a SNOTEL site
• Uses multiple facts from the notes accurately

Why the other choices are wrong

The data collected by SNOTEL sites…
• Describes function, not an example.

Snow hydrologist Julie Koeberle helps maintain…
• Describes a person’s role, not a site.

Located throughout Wyoming…
• General description, no specific example.

question:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• The nautical mile (6,076 feet) is the measure of distance used in seafaring navigation.
• A nautical mile directly correlates to one minute (1/60th of a degree) of latitude.
• The curvature of Earth affects the accurate measurement of long distances when using flat maps.
• Measuring distances with latitude and longitude coordinates takes into account Earth’s curvature.
• Mariners use nautical charts marked with latitude and longitude to quickly calculate distances and positions.

The student wants to explain why nautical miles are used to measure distances in seafaring navigation. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
choices: Nautical miles are a measure of distance equal to one minute of latitude, which is a feature nautical charts use to calculate distances and positions.

Nautical charts use latitude and longitude to measure long distances; these charts are more accurate than flat maps for measuring distances in seafaring navigation because they account for Earth’s curvature.
Since they directly correlate to the coordinates on nautical charts, which take into account Earth’s curvature, nautical miles are an efficient way to calculate distances at sea.
Using nautical miles for navigation at sea takes Earth’s curvature into account, whereas measuring distances with latitude and longitude coordinates does not.
explanation:
Correct answer
Since they directly correlate to the coordinates on nautical charts, which take into account Earth’s curvature, nautical miles are an efficient way to calculate distances at sea.

Why this is correct
The goal is to explain why nautical miles are used in seafaring navigation.

This choice:
• Links nautical miles to latitude/longitude
• Explains the role of Earth’s curvature
• Connects directly to navigation efficiency

It synthesizes multiple notes into a clear explanation.

Why the other choices are wrong

Nautical miles are equal to one minute of latitude…
• True, but incomplete; it doesn’t explain why they are used.

Nautical charts are more accurate than flat maps…
• Shifts focus to charts rather than nautical miles.

Using nautical miles takes Earth’s curvature into account, whereas measuring distances with latitude and longitude does not.
• Factually incorrect: latitude and longitude do account for curvature.

Vertical gene transfer involves the transmission of genetic material from a parent to offspring; horizontal gene transfer, on the other hand, involves the exchange of genetic material between organisms not in a parent-offspring relationship. <u>While horizontal gene transfer is common among prokaryotes—single-celled organisms, such as the bacteria Brevibacillus borstelensis and Lactococcus lactis—it has rarely been observed among eukaryotes (multicellular organisms).</u> However, new studies suggest that horizontal gene transfer is more common in eukaryotes than originally thought.

Which choice best states the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
choices: It indicates a distinction between the mechanics of two kinds of biological processes.
It contrasts the frequency with which a biological phenomenon has been detected in two categories of organisms.
It explains why a common perception of a biological process is flawed.
It argues that two biological phenomena are more similar than they may initially appear to be.
explanation:
Correct answer: B — It contrasts the frequency with which a biological phenomenon has been detected in two categories of organisms.

Why:
The underlined sentence explicitly compares how often horizontal gene transfer occurs in two groups:

it is common among prokaryotes, and

it has been rarely observed among eukaryotes.

That is a direct contrast in frequency of occurrence across two categories of organisms, which is exactly what choice B states.

Why the other choices don’t work (briefly):

A focuses on mechanics (how the processes work), but the mechanics were explained earlier; the underlined sentence is about how often it happens.

C describes correcting a misconception, which happens in the following sentence (“However, new studies suggest…”), not in the underlined one.

D claims the sentence argues the phenomena are similar, but the sentence actually emphasizes a difference, not a similarity.

question:
In a study by Mika R. Moran, Daniel A. Rodriguez, and colleagues, residents of Bogotá, Colombia, and Fortaleza, Brazil, were surveyed about parks in their cities. Of the 1,121 respondents from Bogotá, 71.9% indicated that they use the city's parks, and of the 938 respondents from Fortaleza, 35.7% indicated using city parks. Given that the percentage of Bogotá respondents who reported living within a 10-minute walk of a park was much lower than that reported by Fortaleza respondents, greater proximity alone can't explain the difference in park use.

The text makes which point about the difference between the proportions of Bogotá residents and Fortaleza residents using parks?
choices: It is caused by something other than the parks' proximity to city residents.
It was calculated using sources that predate the survey.
It was much larger than the researchers conducting the study expected.
It could be due to inaccuracies in the survey results.
explanation:
Correct answer: A — It is caused by something other than the parks' proximity to city residents.

Why A is correct:
The text explicitly states that greater proximity alone can’t explain the difference in park use because Bogotá residents live closer to parks less often than Fortaleza residents, yet use parks more often. That directly implies another factor must be causing the difference.

Why the others are wrong:

B: Nothing is said about sources predating the survey.

C: The text gives no indication of researchers’ expectations.

D: The text treats the data as valid; it does not suggest inaccuracies.

question:
In a study by Mika R. Moran, Daniel A. Rodriguez, and colleagues, residents of Caracas, Venezuela, and Fortaleza, Brazil, were surveyed about parks in their cities. Of the 1,043 respondents from Caracas, 44.7% indicated that they use the city's parks, and of the 938 respondents from Fortaleza, 35.7% indicated using city parks. <u>It may be tempting to assume the difference is due to different levels of access to parks;</u> however, given that the percentage of Caracas respondents who reported living within a 10-minute walk of a park was much lower than that reported by Fortaleza respondents, greater proximity alone can't explain the difference in park use.

Which choice best describes the function of the underlined portion in the text as a whole?
choices: It introduces a counterexample to the scenario described earlier in the text.
It provides context to help understand the scope of the researchers' survey.
It marks a shift from a discussion of the researchers' conclusion to a discussion of their methods.
It presents a potential explanation for the team's findings that the text goes on to refute.
explanation:
Correct answer: D — It presents a potential explanation for the team's findings that the text goes on to refute.

Why D is correct:
The underlined sentence introduces an idea that seems reasonable (“the difference is due to access to parks”), and the word “however” signals that this explanation is about to be rejected. The following clause then directly refutes it.

Why the others are wrong:

A: A counterexample would contradict a prior claim with evidence, not introduce a tempting but flawed explanation.

B: The sentence does not give background or scope; it proposes a hypothesis.

C: There is no shift to methods—only from possible explanation to refutation.

question:
Psychologists Gregory Bryant, Dorsa Amir, and colleagues investigated cross-cultural perceptions of spontaneous (real) laughter and volitional (fake or forced) laughter. Study participants from 21 societies, including those in Austria and Turkey, listened to randomized recordings of 18 spontaneous laughs taken from natural conversations between pairs of women and 18 volitional laughs produced separately by 18 different women in response to an experimenter's instruction to laugh. Analysis of the participants' evaluations of the laughs prompted the team to conclude that the ability to distinguish between spontaneous and volitional laughter appears to be universal across cultures.

Which quotation from a psychologist not involved in the team's study would most directly weaken the team's conclusion?
choices: “When an individual chooses to produce volitional laughter in a natural social context, the laughter often shares certain acoustic qualities, such as pitch and fluctuation of intensity, with spontaneous laughter.”

“Although the team considered the average size of communities in each society in the study, that demographic factor was found to have no effect on listeners' identifications of laughter as spontaneous or volitional.”
“Judgments of spontaneous laughter are often associated with acoustic features such as greater intensity variability and higher pitch.”
“Recent studies in communications have shown that certain acoustic features of spontaneous laughter, such as pitch and intensity, are consistent both within and across societies.”
explanation:
Correct answer: A

Why A weakens the conclusion:
The team concludes that the ability to distinguish real from fake laughter is universal across cultures. Choice A says that volitional laughter can share key acoustic qualities with spontaneous laughter in natural contexts. If fake laughter can closely resemble real laughter, then listeners’ ability to distinguish between them may not be reliable or universal, directly undermining the conclusion.

Why the others don’t weaken:

B: Says a demographic factor had no effect—this supports the study’s robustness.

C: Describes features associated with spontaneous laughter—this aligns with the team’s findings.

D: Says features are consistent across societies—this reinforces the idea of universality.

question:
Text 1

The island of Grande Terre split from the former supercontinent Gondwana around 80 million years ago, carrying Gondwanan species from a variety of clades with it. The island was periodically submerged until 37 million years ago, but some researchers suggest that its current biota includes species from clades predating the split that took refuge on islands near Grande Terre during submergence events and then returned.

Text 2

Thomas R. Buckley et al. found that the crown age—the age of the most recent common ancestor of all species in the clade (i.e., the clade's founder)—of Grande Terre's clade of stick insects is 41.1 million years, which is among the oldest clade crown ages of species inhabiting the island today. Nearly all of Grande Terre's living species belong to clades that originated much more recently; for example, the crown age of the island's clade of Goodeniaceae plants is 2.0 million years.

Based on the texts, the author of Text 2 would most likely agree with which statement about the "Gondwanan species" discussed in Text 1?
choices: Most of them began recolonizing Grande Terre from nearby islands around 2.0 million years ago.
Clades to which they belong originated no earlier than 41.1 million years ago.
Few, if any, of them were members of a clade that includes species currently inhabiting Grande Terre.
Although most of them have living descendants on Grande Terre, the stick insects and Goodeniaceae plants do not.
explanation:
Correct answer: C

Why C is correct:
Text 2 emphasizes that nearly all living species on Grande Terre belong to much younger clades, with only rare exceptions (e.g., stick insects at 41.1 million years). This suggests that very few, if any, present-day species belong to ancient Gondwanan clades, matching choice C.

Why the others are wrong:

A: Incorrectly ties recolonization to 2.0 million years; that number refers only to Goodeniaceae plants.

B: Overgeneralizes from the oldest clade (41.1 million years) to all Gondwanan species.

D: Flatly contradicts Text 2, which explicitly says stick insects do belong to one of the oldest clades.

question:
Saeed M.Z.A. Tarabieh conducted a study of consumer attitudes toward Jordanian food and beverage companies and found that for consumers who value environmental conservation, their likelihood of purchasing a product decreased when their perception of the product's risk of causing environmental harm increased. Subsequently, other researchers conducted a study of various demographic groups in Chile, investigating participants' intentions to purchase a new mobile phone, and found that, on average, college students had the lowest perception among all the demographic groups in the study of the environmental risks of the mobile phone. Assuming that the results of Tarabieh's study are broadly applicable, this finding suggests that ________.

Which choice most logically completes the text?
choices: college students might be more likely than participants in the other demographic groups to purchase the mobile phone.
college students likely prioritize other factors over a product's environmental sustainability when making purchasing decisions.
there is not a meaningful difference in the average likelihood of purchasing environmentally friendly products among the demographic groups included in the study.
the new mobile phone is less appealing to college students than other similar products on the market are.
explanation:
Correct answer: A — college students might be more likely than participants in the other demographic groups to purchase the mobile phone.

Why A is correct:
Tarabieh’s study shows a clear relationship: for people who value environmental conservation, higher perceived environmental risk → lower likelihood of purchase.
The Chile study finds that college students perceive the lowest environmental risk of the phone. If Tarabieh’s findings apply broadly, then lower perceived risk corresponds to higher likelihood of purchase, meaning college students would be more likely to buy the phone than other groups.

Why the other choices are wrong:

B: This claims something about college students’ values, but the studies only address perceived risk, not what factors students prioritize.

C: The text actually implies a difference in likelihood (via differences in perceived risk), not a lack of one.

D: This contradicts the logic of the findings; lower perceived risk would make the phone more, not less, appealing.

Key SAT logic move:
Translate the relationship → apply it to the new group → choose the option that directly follows from that relationship, without adding assumptions.

question:
When Anglo and African Americans moved West in the nineteenth century to begin cattle ranching, they learned the trade from Spanish-speaking Mexican vaqueros (cowboys). This is why many ranching terms come from _______ English word “lasso” (a rope) comes from the Spanish word lazo, and “cinch” (a belt) comes from cincho.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

HINT

For questions that test sentence structure and boundaries, I always start with a hard stop (meaning an answer choice that ends a sentence). In this case, that means A) and D).

The poem "The Ballad of Rudolph Reed," which was published in 1960, contains three signature elements of Gwendolyn Brooks's poetic ___ compressed lines infused with bursts of vivid imagery; syncopated rhythms, largely inspired by the blues tradition; and a keen attention to everyday life in Brooks's South Side Chicago neighborhood.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

HINT

While 95% of the time, semicolons act like a period to end a sentence, 5% of the time, they show up as punctuation to separate phrases that have a comma baked into the listed phrases.

Here, the testmaker lists out 3 things after the colon:

• terse, compressed lines infused with bursts of vivid imagery
• syncopated rhythms, largely inspired by the blues tradition
• a keen attention to everyday life in Brooks's South Side Chicago neighborhood

Since list 1 and list 2 have commas in it, the semicolon should be used to separate the 3 list of phrases.

Also note the underlined part of the sentence:
"...the blues tradition<u>; and</u> a keen attention..."

See the semi colon + and? you can't start a sentence with "and" so you would have to deduce that the paragraph is trying to list items.

Watch for this as it is becoming a trending problem on the 2025-2026 tests.

Should the Czech Republic cut taxes? As of 2017, the Czech Republic’s top tax rate (46%) was lower than the highest point on the country’s Laffer curve. A theoretical relationship between tax rates and revenues, the curve can be used to determine whether tax cuts will ultimately increase a country’s tax revenue, according to some ______ 2017 data suggested that the Czech Republic was below the threshold for a tax cut.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

HINT

For questions that test sentence structure and boundaries, I always start with a hard stop (meaning an answer choice that ends a sentence). In this case, that means A) and D).

First check to see if before the hardstop, we have a complete sentence. We do here, so we proceed.

Then I simply read the rest of the sentence to see if it's a complete sentence, which means the hard stop is correct...

or

...to see if it's incomplete, where then I would determine what type of phrase I need (dependent clause, modifier, etc).

In this case, if I choose A), then I have the following left:

• 2017 data suggested that the Czech Republic was below the threshold for a tax cut.
This is a complete sentence, so the period hardstop works.

Most of the time, the hardstop is the correct answer and will save you time.
explanation: A period properly ends the clause about economists, creating two complete and correctly punctuated sentences.

question:

In a 2022 study, researchers studying connections between the physical location in which a social media post was ______ analyzed geotagged social media posts from various locations in Chicago. They found that posts from the city’s parks contained more words associated with happiness than other posts did.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation:
It's easier to explain this one if I break the sentence down:

Phrase Phrase

• In a 2022 study,

Main Sentence

• researchers studying connections...analyzed geotagged social media posts from various locations in Chicago.

Prep Phrase

question:
With an installed capacity of 35 megawatts, the Platanares geothermal power plant in Honduras offers a dependable source of renewable energy. Power plants like Platanares supply only a small fraction of Honduras’s _____ the scarcity of sites with the necessary combination of high-temperature geothermal reservoirs and fractured rock limit the widespread development of such systems.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation:
First, always start with the hard stops.

If we stop the sentence here, then the first and second parts can stand alone.

• Power plants like Platanares supply only a small fraction of Honduras’s electricity;
• the scarcity of sites with the necessary combination of high-temperature geothermal reservoirs and fractured rock limit the widespread development of such systems.

Now, we have to deal with the "though" transition.

• What are we contrasting here? The 1st and 2nd sentence? or the 2nd and 3rd sentence?
• 1st and 2nd:

• With an installed capacity of 35 megawatts, the Platanares geothermal power plant in Honduras offers a dependable source of renewable energy.
• Power plants like Platanares supply only a small fraction of Honduras’s electricity.

• 2nd and 3rd:

• Power plants like Platanares supply only a small fraction of Honduras’s electricity;
• the scarcity of sites with the necessary combination of high-temperature geothermal reservoirs and fractured rock limit the widespread development of such systems.

The 1st and 2nd seem like a contrast while the 2nd and 3rd seem like supportive sentences. So the "though" needs to be placed in the 2nd sentence. B) does this.

question:
Uncle Vanya: Scenes from Country Life in Four Acts is an 1898 play by Anton Chekhov, originally written in Russian. In the play, Professor Serebrakoff and his wife Helena have come to stay at their country estate, which Vanya manages with the help of Sonia, the professor's daughter from a previous marriage. Chekhov depicts Vanya's opinion of Professor Serebrakoff as having changed significantly, as is evident when __________

Which quotation from a translation of Uncle Vanya most effectively illustrates the claim?

HINT:

The last part of these questions are the most important as they direct you to find particular details in the quotes below.

Here, they want you find Vanya's opinion of Serebrakoff <u>having changed significantly.</u>

The correct answer should reflect this.
choices: Vanya says to Professor Serebrakoff, "For twenty-five years I have managed [the country estate], and have sent you the returns from it like the most honest of servants, and you have never given me one single word of thanks for my work, not one-neither in my youth nor now.”
Professor Serebrakoff says to Helena, "It is funny that everybody listens to [Vanya] and his old idiot of a mother, but the moment I open my lips you all begin to feel ill-treated.”

Vanya says to Professor Serebrakoff, "This place [the country estate] could never have been bought had I not renounced my inheritance in favor of my sister [the professor's late wife], whom I deeply loved-and what is more, I worked for ten years like an ox, and paid off the debt.”

Vanya says to himself, "I was proud of [Professor Serebrakoff] and of his learning; I received all his words and writings as inspired and now? Now he has retired,and what is the total of his life? A blank! He is absolutely unknown,and his fame has burst like a soap-bubble.I have been deceived; I see that now, basely deceived.”
explanation:
Why D is correct:

The question asks for evidence that Vanya’s opinion of Professor Serebrakoff has changed significantly. Choice D directly shows this shift in attitude. Vanya explicitly contrasts his past admiration—when he was “proud” of the professor and viewed his work as “inspired”—with his current disillusionment, calling the professor’s life “a blank” and saying he has been “basely deceived.” This quotation clearly demonstrates a transformation from respect and reverence to bitterness and regret, making it the most effective illustration of the claim.

Why the other answers are wrong (brief)
❌ A Wrong because: It shows resentment, but does not explicitly contrast Vanya’s past and present views.

❌ B Wrong because: It reflects the professor’s opinion of Vanya, not Vanya’s opinion of the professor.

❌ C Wrong because: It focuses on Vanya’s sacrifices, not a change in his view of Professor Serebrakoff.

question:
Veronica L. Bura, Akito Y. Kawahara, and Jayne E. Yack investigated the evolution and function of sound production in silk moth and hawk moth caterpillars. They found that during harmless simulated attacks on isolated caterpillars, 33% of the tested species produced sound, which ranged from clicks in Actias luna to whistles in Phyllosphingia dissimilis. Although some insects use sound to communicate with members of the same species, the researchers claim that the caterpillar sounds recorded in their study are directed primarily at predators.

Which finding, if true, would most directly support Bura and colleagues' claim?

HINT:

These are "if true" questions so focus on the claim: Caterpillar sounds are directed primarily at predators, not for communication with other caterpillars.

Since you're looking to support or strengthen the claim, you’ll need evidence that:
• sounds are triggered by attacks, and
• sounds are not used outside predator contexts

Make note of the "the caterpillar sounds recorded in their study", which were clicks and whistles, so both have to be addressed.
choices: None of the species that emitted sounds did so before the simulated attacks, and nearly all stopped emitting sounds within ten seconds after the attacks.
Caterpillar clicks were emitted in a frequency detectable by birds that prey on caterpillars, but caterpillar whistles were not.
Each caterpillar species tended to produce one sound during simulated attacks, although individuals occasionally made a variety of other sounds during simulated attacks as well.
In most cases, the sound that a caterpillar species produced during simulated attacks was not produced by other caterpillar species during simulated attacks.
explanation:
Why the correct answer works (A)

Choice A shows:
• sounds happen only during attacks
• sounds stop right after attacks

That strongly suggests the sounds are a defensive response, not communication.

This is behavioral timing logic:
If behavior only happens during threat → it’s probably anti-predator.

Main trap in this question

Answers that describe:
• sound variety
• sound differences among species
• sound mechanics

Those are interesting, but they don’t prove purpose.

question:
Veronica L.Bura, Akito Y.Kawahara, and Jayne E. Yack investigated the function of sound production in silk moth and hawk moth caterpillars. They found that during harmless simulated attacks, 33% of the tested species produced sound, which included four distinct types: chirps, whistles, vocalizations, and clicks. In addition, Antheraea polyphemus and Antheraea polyphemus oculea released a chemical while or after producing the first sound. These species exclusively produced clicks and chirps, which tend to be shorter in duration than whistles and vocalizations. Bura and colleagues argue that clicks and chirps in species that use chemical defenses are primarily a means of warning (i.e., "educating") predators rather than frightening or startling them.

Which finding, if true, would most directly support Bura and colleagues' claim?

HINT:

These are "if true" questions so focus on the claim: Clicks and chirps function as warning signals (educating predators), not as startle sounds.

Since you're looking to support or strengthen the claim, you’ll need evidence that:
• predators can perceive the sounds
• the sounds are suited for learning/association, not shock
choices: Short-duration sounds like clicks and chirps tend to be especially effective in training animals to associate a behavior with a consequence.
Caterpillars that use chemical defenses produced sounds at a higher volume than did caterpillars without chemical defenses.
The acoustic characteristics of clicks and chirps make them particularly audible to bats, lizards, and birds, some of the most frequent predators of caterpillars.
Chickens and yellow warblers, two predators of caterpillars, have been observed to stop their attacks in response to caterpillar sounds of any duration.
explanation:
Why the correct answer works (C)

Choice C shows:
• clicks/chirps are audible to predators

If predators can hear them clearly, the sounds can function as signals that predators learn to associate with danger.

This is mechanism alignment logic:
A warning signal must be detectable by the target audience.

Main trap in this question

Confusing:
• effectiveness in stopping attacks
with
• effectiveness as warning vs startle

For example, “predators stop attacking” (choice D) does NOT distinguish:
warning vs fear — both could cause stopping.

A) is wrong bc the claim strictly limits the results/consequences to warning instead of frightening or startling, but A) is saying any consequence in general, which makes it untrue. Remember that if even one word in an answer choice is wrong, the entire thing is wrong.

C) gives a minimum amount of support to strengthen the claim, but it does strengthen it. So it is not wrong even if it strengthens the claim by only a little, making it correct.

question:
Veronica L. Bura, Akito Y. Kawahara, and Jayne E. Yack investigated the evolution and function of sound production in silk moth and hawk moth caterpillars. They found that during harmless simulated attacks on caterpillars, 33% of the tested species produced sound, which ranged from clicks in Antheraea polyphemus to chirps in Schausiella santarosensis. A second research team has claimed that caterpillars use these sounds primarily to communicate with other members of their species.

Which finding, if true, would most directly challenge the second team's claim?

HINT:

These are "if true" questions so focus on the claim: Caterpillars use sounds primarily to communicate with members of their own species.

Since you're looking to <u>WEAKEN </u>the claim, you’ll need evidence that:
• communication with others is unlikely or impossible
choices: The sounds caterpillars produced in response to the simulated attacks lacked acoustic characteristics that would make them audible to bats, lizards, or birds, some of the most frequent predators of caterpillars.
Most of the caterpillar species that were found to not produce sound in response to simulated attacks have been observed producing sound during encounters with other members of their species.

Among the caterpillar species that produced sound in response to simulated attacks, no individuals produced sound in the minute before the attacks, but the vast majority of individuals produced sound once the simulated attacks began.
Caterpillars that were found to produce sounds in response to simulated attacks are typically solitary and were tested in isolation.
explanation:
Why the correct answer works (D)

Choice D shows:
• caterpillars were solitary
• tested in isolation

If they’re alone, then sound cannot be for communication with other caterpillars.

This is feasibility logic:
If there’s no audience, communication can’t be the function.

Main trap in this question

Choosing answers that say:
• sounds occur during attacks
• sounds don’t occur before attacks

Those support predator-directed sound, but they don’t directly rule out communication.

question:
[image 0/12189505_IPP3AL7B.jpg]
Neuroscientist Kiyohito Iigaya and colleagues developed a computational model to predict how much a person will enjoy a particular work of art on a scale from 1 (not at all) to 4 (very much). They then recruited participants to use the same scale to rate several sets of paintings in various styles and calculated the correlation between the ratings predicted by the model and those reported by the participants. Assuming participant P6 gave equal ratings to the abstract and cubist paintings, the data in the graph indicate the model predicted that __________

Which choice most effectively uses data from the graph to complete the example?

HINT:

Answer D) is a trap, which talks about how much P6 liked one style compared to the other.

So for D to be correct, the graph would need to show relative enjoyment levels.

However, the graph is measuring correlation: how closely the model’s predictions match the participant’s actual ratings.

Important:

• It does NOT show how much someone enjoyed the paintings.
• It does NOT show higher vs lower preference.
• It does NOT show which style was liked more.

It ONLY shows:

• How well the model predicted that person’s ratings for that style.
choices: P6's rating for abstract and cubist paintings would equal one another.
P6's ratings for abstract and cubist paintings would differ from one another.
P6 would derive less aesthetic pleasure from abstract paintings than from cubist paintings.
P6 would derive more aesthetic pleasure from abstract paintings than from cubist paintings.
explanation:
The graph’s y-axis is labeled correlation, which measures how closely the model’s predicted ratings matched the participant’s actual ratings, not how much the participant enjoyed the paintings.

The question states that participant P6 gave equal ratings to abstract and cubist paintings. However, the graph shows that for P6, the correlation values differ between abstract and cubist styles. This indicates that the model’s predictions for P6 were not equally accurate for the two styles.

Because the correlations are different, the model must have predicted different ratings for abstract and cubist paintings, even though P6 actually rated them the same. Therefore, the data indicate that the model predicted P6’s ratings for abstract and cubist paintings would differ from one another.

Choices C and D are incorrect because they make claims about aesthetic pleasure or preference, which the graph does not measure. Correlation reflects predictive accuracy, not enjoyment level.

Assuming participant P1 gave equal ratings to the impressionist and color-field paintings, the data in the graph suggest that the model predicted that __________

question:
Like all species of baleen whales, the pygmy right whale feeds on tiny creatures known as krill by filtering water through bristlelike keratin structures called baleen plates. In this way, baleen whales can eat up to 30 percent of their total mass per day. And while no one would call the pygmy right whale small—it can have a mass as high as 3,500 kg—it is one of the smaller baleen whales and is much smaller than the bowhead whale, which can weigh a whopping 66,000 kg and consume as much as 19,800 kg of krill per day.

choices: The bowhead whale is able to eat more krill per day than the pygmy right whale is.

Proto-Atlantic-Congo — a protolanguage, or ancestral language of a family or descendant (daughter) language — is said to be the common ancestor of all Atlantic-Congo languages. This designation is _____ Proto-Atlantic-Congo is only postulated, its characteristics being inferred from the linguistic properties of its 1,453 daughters.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

HINT:

I call these Sentence Structure Transition questions or SST's.

First, always start with the hard stops.

• This designation is hypothetical:
• roto-Atlantic-Congo is only postulated, its characteristics being inferred from the linguistic properties of its 1,453 daughters.
• Can I separate these two sentences? Yes.

Next, acknowledge the 3 sentences in this problem:

• Proto-Atlantic-Congo is said to be the common ancestor of all Atlantic-Congo languages.
• This designation is hypothetical:
• Proto-Atlantic-Congo is only postulated, its characteristics being inferred from the linguistic properties of its 1,453 daughters.

Then, deal with the transition word. Here it's "however," which is a contrast word so I have to find the two sentences that contrast each other:

• Sentence 1 and 2 seem to be contradictory in nature
• Sentence 3 is expanding on sentence 2's assertion that the designation is hypothetical (in sentence 3, postulated means hypothesized).

Therefore, I can conclude that I need to have the word "however" in the second sentence. Only A does this.

Subject Verb Agreement (SVA) – Concept Notes

Subject verb agreement means that the verb in a sentence must match the subject in number. If the subject is singular, the verb must be singular. If the subject is plural, the verb must be plural.

Basic Rule for SVA

Singular Subject
When the subject is singular, the verb usually ends in s.

• Example

• The cat runs after the dog.
• Explanation
• The subject is cat.
• Cat is singular.
• Therefore, the verb must be runs, which ends in s.

Plural Subject
When the subject is plural, the verb usually does not end in s.

• Example

• The cats run after the dog.
• Explanation
• The subject is cats.
• Cats is plural.
• Therefore, the verb must be run, which does not end in s.

Lesson Summary

• Singular subject → verb ends in s
• Plural subject → verb does not end in s

Modifiers

For SAT purposes, you will need to know modifiers for SVA and for Sentence Structure problems.

BUT FIRST, you'll need to learn what they are and how to identify them!

Modifiers are like descriptive phrases for nouns.
Modifiers provide additional details for nouns.

Example
Original sentence - After studying for hours, the students learned the new concept.
Main sentence - The students learned the new concept
Modifier - After studying for hours

• Here, "after studying for hours" provides additional details for the noun "the students" since it tells us what they did. Therefore, it is a descriptive phrase—aka modifier.

Example
Original sentence - The wolf that was hungry ran after the rabbit fiercely.
Main sentence - The wolf ran after the rabbit fiercely
Modifier - that was hungry

• Here, "that was hungry" provides additional details for the noun "the wolf."

Example
Original sentence - Many people have been waiting for the Tesla Roadster, an electric car that can go 0 to 60 mph in 1.9 seconds.
Main sentence - Many people have been waiting for the Tesla Roadster
Modifier - an electric car that can go 0 to 60 mph in 1.9 seconds

• Here, "an electric car that can go 0 to 60 mph in 1.9 seconds" provides additional details for the noun "the Tesla Roadster."

Types of Modifiers

• Gerund Phrases

• Gerunds are words that end in -ing.
• Example: "Running down the street, the dog barked loudly."

• Infinitive Verb Phrases

• Begin with "to" + base form of a verb and function as adjectives or adverbs.
• Example: "To win the race, she trained every day."

• Appositive Phrases

• Rename or explain a noun.
• Example: "My friend, a skilled pianist, gave a recital.

• "That" Relative Clauses

• Begin with the word "that."
• Example: "The book that she wrote became a bestseller."

• Interrogative Pronouns

• Begin with an interrogative pronoun, BUT in the middle of the sentence (who, when, where, which).
• Example: "The book, which she wrote, became a bestseller."

• Noun Phrase

• usually starts with a, an, the
• Example 1: Denise, a former lawyer, went on to work for several start up companies.
• Example 2: "My friend bought a Tesla Roadster, the car that goes fast."

• Past Tense Verb

• Past tense verb + noun phrase, creating participial or adjective phrases
• Example 1: Having studied all night, the students did well on the test.
• Example 2: Sarah, overcome with grief, began to tear up.
• Example 3: Made with all natural ingredients, the homemade pizza was the best that Ben ever had.

Inverted Subject-Verb Agreement (SVA)

Inverted Subject-Verb Agreement (SVA) occurs when the usual order of a sentence is flipped, so the verb comes before the subject. Normally, we expect the sentence to follow a Subject --> Verb order, like in the sentence "The dog barks." However, in an inverted SVA structure, the verb is placed at the beginning, and the subject follows it.

This inversion is commonly used in:

• Existential constructions with "there" or "here."
• Prepositional phrases at the beginning of the sentence.

Let’s look at two common instances of inverted SVA:

1. "There" or "Here" Sentences:
In these sentences, "there" or "here" is used at the beginning to introduce the existence or location of something, and the verb comes first, followed by the subject.

• Example:

• Sentence: There is/are a large group of students waiting in line.
• Explanation: The word "there" serves as a placeholder, and the actual subject ("a large group of students") comes after the verb. Since "group" is singular, the verb must also be singular. Therefore, "is" is the correct form.
• Answer: There is a large group of students waiting in line.

What to look out for:
"There" or "Here" will often start the sentence, followed by the verb, with the actual subject coming later.
Check if the subject is singular or plural to determine the correct verb.

2. Prepositional Phrases at the Beginning, followed by the Verb:
In this case, the sentence begins with a prepositional phrase, <u>followed by the verb</u>. The prepositional phrase adds context but is not part of the subject.

• Example:

• Sentence: On the top shelf rests a stack of books.
• Explanation: The prepositional phrase "On the top shelf" comes at the beginning. The real subject, "a stack of books," comes after the verb. "Stack" is singular, so the verb must be singular as well. Therefore, "rests" is the correct verb form.
• Answer: On the top shelf rests a stack of books.

• What to look out for

• The prepositional phrase ("On the top shelf") comes first, which might make it seem like the subject and verb order is different.
• After crossing out the prepositional phrase, the subject will follow the verb. Identify whether the subject is singular or plural to use the correct verb.

• If the Prepositional Phrase is at the beginning, but is followed by a comma, then it is NOT an inverted sentence. It is a typical Subject-Verb agreement structure where the sentence is just starting with a prep phrase.

• Example:

• On the top shelf, the cat sleeps peacefully.
• Explanation: the prep phrase "On the top shelf" is followed by a comma, not a verb. Therefore, it is a regular subject-verb construction and NOT an inverted SVA construction.
• The subject = the cat
• Therefore, "sleeps" is the correct verb form.

Key Takeaway
By identifying these patterns, you can correctly apply subject-verb agreement, even when the subject appears after the verb! Always remember to look for the actual subject after the verb to determine whether it’s singular or plural.

Subject-Verb Agreement with Conjunctions

Rule 1: Subject-Verb Agreement with Conjunctions Connecting Two Subjects
When two subjects are connected by "and", the subject is treated as plural, and the verb must be in the plural form.

• Example: Two Subjects Connected by "And"

• Sentence: Tom and Jerry are best friends.
• Explanation: "Tom" and "Jerry" are two subjects joined by "and," making the subject plural.
• The verb "are" is plural to agree with the plural subject.

• Answer: Tom and Jerry are best friends.

Rule 2: Subject-Verb Agreement with Conjunctions Connecting Two Independent Clauses
When two independent clauses are connected by "and", the subject of each clause must agree with its respective verb. The verb in each clause must be in the form that matches the subject of that clause.

• Example: Two Independent Clauses Connected by "And"

• Sentence: He likes to run in the morning, and he likes to work out at night.
• Explanation: The sentence contains two independent clauses:
• "He likes to run in the morning" (subject "he" is singular, so the verb "likes" is singular).
• "He likes to work out at night" (subject "he" is singular, so the verb "likes" is singular).
• Both subjects ("he") are singular, and the verbs in both clauses ("likes") are singular to match the singular subject.

• Answer: He likes to run in the morning, and he likes to work out at night.

Key Takeaways

• Conjunction connecting two subjects: When two subjects are connected by "and", the subject is treated as plural, and you must use a plural verb.
• Conjunction connecting two independent clauses: When two independent clauses are connected by "and", each subject in the clauses must agree with its verb. The verb should match the number (singular or plural) of the subject in each clause.

Modifier Placement Rule

Modifiers must appear near the nouns they describe to avoid confusion.

• Example 1: The car, speeding down the highway, was a blur.

• The modifier "speeding down the highway" is placed after "the car" to show that it is providing more details about the car.

• Example 2: Speeding down the highway, the car was a blur.

• The modifier "speeding down the highway" starts the sentence, so "the car" can only be placed after the modifier and comma. This is a structure the SAT test makers create.

The Exception to the Modifier Placement Rule

• The Exception Rule kicks in when all of these conditions are met:

• the modifier is placed at the end of an independent clause/sentence
• there is a comma before the modifier
• the modifier is a gerund phrase

• Example: The car was a blur, <u>speeding down the highway</u>.

• The modifier "speeding down the highway" comes after the sentence, and the key here is that there is a comma before the modifier.
• This is an exception to the main rule that modifiers need to be placed as close to the noun as possible.

Subject-Verb Agreement with Indefinite Subjects

When words such as everybody, each, neither, either, anyone, no one, anybody, and similar indefinite pronouns are used as the subject of a sentence, they are treated as singular subjects, and the verb must also be singular.

Explanation

• Indefinite pronouns like everybody, each, nobody, anyone, no one, and similar words refer to a singular entity, even if they sound plural.
• These words require a singular verb, regardless of the plural idea they might seem to express.

Examples and Explanations

1. Example with "Everybody"

• Sentence: Everybody loves Simon.
• Explanation: The word "everybody" refers to a singular group of people, but it is treated as a singular subject.
• Since it is singular, we use the singular verb "loves."
• Answer: Everybody loves Simon.

2. Example with "Each"

• Sentence: Each of the boys has an hour to respond.
• Explanation: "Each" is singular, so even though it refers to multiple candidates, it takes a singular verb ("has") in this sentence.
• Answer: Each of the boys has an hour to respond.

3. Example with "Neither"

• Sentence: Neither of the girls wants to respond.
• Explanation: "Neither" is a singular subject, even though it might refer to two candidates.
• The verb must agree with the singular subject, so we use "wants."
• Answer: Neither of the girls wants to respond.

Exceptions

1. When you have "Neither...nor..."

• When you have "Neither" without the "nor" then "Neither" will serve as a singular subject.
• But if you have "Neither' followed by "nor" then you will need to look at the noun that follows the "nor" and treat that as the subject.

• Example 1

• Neither the boy nor <u>the girls</u> (likes/like) chocolate.
• Here, "the girls" follows "nor" so the subject will be "the girls."

• Example 2

• Neither the girls nor <u>the boy</u> (likes/like) chocolate.
• Here, "the boy" follows "nor" so the subject will be "the boy."

2. The same exception rule applies for "Either...or..."

Key Takeaways

• Indefinite pronouns like everybody, everything, each, anyone, no one, and similar terms are treated as singular subjects.
• These subjects always take a singular verb.
• Even if the subject refers to multiple things (e.g., "everybody"), the subject is still considered singular in grammar, so the verb should be in its singular form.
