Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

A bias toward studying animals over plants was one of the many shortcomings researcher Sonia Llorente-Culebras and her team ______ analyzing nearly 400 biodiversity studies from around the globe.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

Lines of code written in Fortran, a programming language used for processing scientific data, ______ translated into executable commands by a tool called a compiler. As a result, Fortran is commonly referred to as a compiled language.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

Zinc and cadmium are among the elements contained in the salty, concentrated brine that remains after seawater is desalinated. Elements can be extracted from this brine in much the same way that materials are mined from the earth. ______ recovering materials from desalination by-products is known as brine mining.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

Charles Ginnever’s steel sculpture Prospect Mountain Project is displayed at Storm King Art Center, an outdoor sculpture park in New York. ______ it endures rain, snow, heat, and humidity. Ginnever’s sculpture is particularly well suited to withstand these elements, though, because it is made of corrosion-resistant steel.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

Many influential studies of British Romanticism by Paul de Man and other scholars have focused on the period’s most prominent poets, such as John Keats, the author of “Ode to Psyche.” A 2022 essay by scholar Stacey McDowell, ______ spotlights a Romantic-era poet whose work, though significant, is less widely known and studied: Ann Yearsley (1753–1806).

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:

• The Yukon River is 1,980 kilometers long.
• It is in North America.
• It ranks No. 23 among the longest rivers in the world.
• The Rhine River is 768 kilometers long.
• It is in Europe.
• It ranks No. 129 among the longest rivers in the world.
The student wants to indicate where the Yukon River is located. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
choices: The Yukon River is located in North America.
The Yukon and Rhine rivers are among the longest rivers in the world.
The Yukon River is 1,980 kilometers long.
The Rhine River is ranked No. 129 among the longest rivers in the world.

question:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:

• An element’s relative abundance in a given environment can be expressed as a mass fraction, mole fraction, or volume fraction.
• Mass fraction is the ratio of an element’s mass to the combined mass of all elements in a given environment.
• The mass fraction of calcium is 17,100 parts per million (ppm) on Earth.
• The mass fraction of strontium is 13 ppm on Earth.
The student wants to compare the relative abundance of calcium on Earth to that of strontium. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
choices: Calcium’s mass relative to the combined mass of all elements on Earth is 17,100 ppm.
The relative abundance of calcium and strontium on Earth can be expressed as a mass fraction, mole fraction, or volume fraction.
On Earth, strontium is far less abundant than calcium, based on the mass fraction of the two elements.
Unlike strontium, calcium has a mass fraction on Earth of 17,100 ppm.

question:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:

• The Carnegie Prize is an international art competition.
• It is administered by the Carnegie Museum of Art in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania.
• One Carnegie Prize gold medal winner is Eduardo Chillida of Spain.
• Chillida’s sculpture Modulation d’espace II was honored in 1964.
The student wants to indicate the name of the artist who created the prize-winning sculpture Modulation d’espace II. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
choices: The Carnegie Prize is an international art competition administered by the Carnegie Museum of Art.
The prize-winning sculpture Modulation d’espace II is by the artist Eduardo Chillida.
In 1964, an artist from Spain won a Carnegie Prize gold medal.
The Carnegie Museum of Art in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania, administers a competition honoring outstanding artworks.

question:
For most of its length, the Paraná River has sufficiently high flow velocity to suspend sedimentary particles, but when the river reaches the calmer waters of the Atlantic Ocean, its channel widens and divides, reducing flow velocity and thereby ______ sedimentary particle suspension. Particles are thus deposited, eventually forming deltaic lobes.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
explanation:
Logic: The river's flow slows as it reaches the ocean, making it easier for sediment to settle. The correct word should mean reducing or hindering the suspension of sediment.

A. Incorrect: Obscuring means hiding, not reducing suspension.
B. Correct: Interrupting means stopping or disrupting sediment suspension.
C. Incorrect: Compounding means increasing, the opposite of the passage.
D. Incorrect: Expediting means speeding up, which would increase suspension.

question:
Writer Lydia Davis observed that while ______ literary forms, such as the poem, are recognizable as such even as they evolve, there are rarer “intergeneric” forms that might, for example, use elements of both fiction and essays to create something unclassifiable. Anne Carson’s long piece Nox arguably fits in this category, since it straddles the line between prose and poetry.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
explanation:
Logic: Davis contrasts familiar literary forms with rare "intergeneric" forms, so the blank should describe forms that are widely accepted and recognizable.

A. Incorrect: Neutral refers to lack of bias, not literary tradition.
B. Incorrect: Equivocal means ambiguous, the opposite of recognizable.
C. Incorrect: Intermediate means in between, which doesn't fit the contrast.
D. Correct: Orthodox means traditional or established, matching the familiar forms.

question:
The subscription model in which consumers who do not deliberately cancel their subscriptions automatically pay recurring fees for access to products and services benefits retailers when consumer ______ is high. Many of the 7.8 percent of subscribers who canceled their fashion and apparel subscriptions in June 2022 had stopped valuing their subscriptions long before then, but sellers profited from those customers’ passivity in the interim.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
explanation:
Logic: Retailers profit when customers do nothing and allow subscriptions to renew automatically. The blank should describe consumers' tendency to remain inactive.

A. Correct: Inertia means a tendency to remain unchanged or inactive.
B. Incorrect: Turnover refers to replacement or change.
C. Incorrect: Decisiveness is the opposite of passivity.
D. Incorrect: Evasion means avoidance, not inactivity.

question:
Founded in New York City in 1904, the Hispanic Society of America is one of the best-known US-based institutions showcasing Latino cultures. Since its founding, it has acquired more than 18,000 objects for its permanent collection. <u>Since 2000, the number of Latino cultural institutions in the US has expanded considerably.</u> LA Plaza de Cultura y Artes, which opened in Los Angeles in 2011 and focuses on Mexican American art and culture, is among the most prominent.

Which choice best states the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
choices: It contrasts the focus of the Latino cultural institution discussed earlier in the text with the focus of the institution discussed later in the text.
It identifies a historical trend of which the Latino cultural institution discussed later in the text is a part.
It describes a historical development that encouraged the founding of the two Latino cultural institutions discussed in the text.
It analyzes how two institutions’ approach to exhibiting artworks reflects the approach taken by most Latino cultural institutions.
explanation:
Logic: The underlined sentence introduces a broader trend, and the following sentence gives one example of that trend.

A. Incorrect: It does not compare the institutions' focuses.
B. Correct: It identifies the historical growth of Latino cultural institutions, of which LA Plaza is an example.
C. Incorrect: The Hispanic Society was founded long before the trend began.
D. Incorrect: The passage never analyzes exhibition methods.

question:
One popular hypothesis concerning animal cognition is that the complexity of species’ social networks is the primary driver of cognitive evolution, an idea addressed by Borgeaud and many others. This view holds that the demand of behaviors related to living in groups—trading grooming for access to food, for example—selects for, and thus accounts for, greater cognition. Now, a growing body of research suggests that interactions between species members without a social connection also present challenges that contribute significantly to sophisticated cognitive adaptations.

Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?
choices: It outlines a widespread view about how behaviors such as trading grooming influence cognitive evolution in animals and then addresses a recent area of study that is relevant to that view.

It identifies the origin of a hypothesis about the effect of trading grooming and other behaviors on cognitive evolution in animals and then indicates that the hypothesis is receiving increasing support from researchers.
It expresses support for an accepted view of social groups and animal behaviors such as trading grooming and then acknowledges emerging findings that seem to undermine that view.
It asserts that the significance of trading grooming in social groups should be reconsidered in light of a new hypothesis and then proposes further study to explore similar animal behaviors.
explanation:
Logic: The passage first explains a widely accepted hypothesis about cognitive evolution, then introduces newer research suggesting an additional factor.

A. Correct: It accurately describes the accepted view followed by relevant new research.
B. Incorrect: The passage doesn't identify who originated the hypothesis or say support is increasing.
C. Incorrect: The author doesn't endorse or reject either position.
D. Incorrect: The passage doesn't propose additional future research.

question:
Text 1
Siberian aster (Eurybia sibirica) plants are native to Alaska, where harsh conditions have historically impeded potential invasive species. As the boreal climate has warmed in recent decades, however, honey clover (Melilotus albus) plants have established themselves in Alaska. Previous research conducted in non-boreal ecosystems has documented warming-induced increases in summer temperatures benefiting invasive species more than native species.

Text 2
At a site near Fairbanks, Alaska, Christa Mulder and Katie Spellman tracked E. sibirica and M. albus, along with other native and invasive species, over several years. They observed that although average summer temperatures were substantially higher in some years of the study than in others, neither E. sibirica nor M. albus showed any significant variation in summer growth patterns from year to year.

Which choice best describes the relationship between the two texts?
choices: Text 2 presents a finding that casts doubt on the generalizability of the research discussed in Text 1.
Text 2 explains a study that suggests an alternative explanation for the trend observed in the research discussed in Text 1.
Text 2 discusses an observation that challenges the validity of the findings described in Text 1.
Text 2 describes a methodology that helps researchers avoid a problem encountered in the studies discussed in Text 1.
explanation:
Logic: Text 1 presents findings from previous research, while Text 2 describes results that do not match those earlier findings, suggesting they may not apply universally.

A. Correct: Text 2 questions whether the earlier findings apply in all ecosystems.
B. Incorrect: Text 2 doesn't offer a different explanation.
C. Incorrect: It doesn't show the earlier research was invalid.
D. Incorrect: The methodology isn't the focus.

question:
In a 2024 study, Corrine Walsh and colleagues examined whether the composition of soil microbial communities could affect plants’ flavor chemistry. Whereas Jimenez-Gomez et al. (2017) showed that adding specific bacterial or fungal strains to soil can yield increased vitamin C in strawberry crops, Walsh and team applied intact microbial communities gathered from ecologically distinct settings across Colorado, including areas of ponderosa pine forest and dry pasture, to mustard plants and evaluated the flavor compounds in the plants’ seeds. This ensured that the microbial conditions in their experiment would better reflect the variation and complexity of naturally occurring communities.

Based on the text, what is the most likely reason Walsh and colleagues chose to avoid the method used in the strawberry study?
choices: The microbial community in the soil from the strawberry study affected plants’ nutrition, not their flavor chemistry.
The microbial community in the soil from the strawberry study likely included similar species to those in wild soils.
The diversity of species of microorganisms in the soil from the strawberry study was already abnormally high before the researchers added further microorganisms.
The composition of microorganisms in the soil in the strawberry study may not have been representative of a naturally existing composition.
explanation:
Logic: Walsh wanted soil conditions that resembled naturally occurring microbial communities, so they avoided adding isolated strains like the earlier study did.

A. Incorrect: The different research topic wasn't the reason for the different method.
B. Incorrect: The passage suggests the opposite.
C. Incorrect: Nothing indicates the strawberry soil already had unusually high diversity.
D. Correct: Adding isolated strains may not reflect the complexity of natural microbial communities.

question:
Information from the Great Sunflower Project helps scientists address pollinator population-size declines caused by habitat loss. Participants monitor which pollinators visit specific plants and the frequency of those visits. Scientists then use this information to determine which plant species best support pollinators and identify where those plant species have declined. Without bees, butterflies, and other pollinators performing their vital role in plant reproduction and food production, ecosystems would suffer—making the conservation efforts informed by this citizen science project all the more important!

According to the text, why is the information collected by the Great Sunflower Project valuable?
choices: It helps project participants demonstrate that butterfly population sizes are growing faster than bee population sizes.
It helps scientists determine which flowers produce the most honey when visited by bees.
It helps gardeners learn how to grow larger sunflowers through better pollination.
It helps scientists develop strategies for addressing pollinator habitat loss.
explanation:
Logic: The project helps scientists determine which plants best support pollinators and where those plants have declined, allowing them to address habitat loss.

A. Incorrect: The project doesn't compare butterfly and bee population growth.
B. Incorrect: Honey production isn't discussed.
C. Incorrect: The project isn't designed to improve gardening.
D. Correct: The data help scientists develop conservation strategies for pollinators.

question:
“The Monster” is an 1898 story by Stephen Crane. In the story, the character of Jimmie is a young boy who has been scolded by his father for accidentally damaging a flower in his garden; Jimmie then looks for sympathy from Henry Johnson, the man responsible for the care of Jimmie’s father’s horses. Crane demonstrates Henry’s tendency towards such sympathy, writing, ______

Which quotation from “The Monster” most effectively illustrates the claim?
choices: “In regard to almost everything in life [Jimmie and Henry] seemed to have minds precisely alike.”

“Henry would sometimes choose to absolutely repudiate [Jimmie’s behavior], and when Jimmie appeared in his shame would bully him most virtuously, preaching with assurance the precepts of [Jimmie’s father’s] creed, and pointing out to Jimmie all of his abominations.”
“For a minute Jimmie refused to take an interest in anything. He was very downcast.”

“Henry... could usually provide a sin to place himself on a footing with the disgraced one. Perhaps he would remember that he had forgotten to put the hitching-strap in the back of the buggy on some recent occasion, and had been reprimanded by [Jimmie’s father].”
explanation:
Logic: The quotation should show Henry expressing sympathy by identifying with Jimmie's mistake rather than judging him.

A. Incorrect: Similar personalities don't demonstrate sympathy.
B. Incorrect: Henry is criticizing Jimmie rather than sympathizing with him.
C. Incorrect: It only describes Jimmie's emotions.
D. Correct: Henry recalls one of his own mistakes to make Jimmie feel less alone.

question:
Describing the adverb as “a word that distracts,” novelist Elmore Leonard is one of several authors and literary critics to recommend minimizing the use of adverbs, especially those ending in -ly (e.g., “grudgingly”), in works of fiction. To investigate the prevalence of -ly adverbs in novels, Ben Blatt used natural language processing—machine learning technology that reads and interprets text—to calculate the rates at which these words occur in both popular fiction and in novels that commonly appear on lists of notable works of English literature, such as Willa Cather’s My Ántonia. Blatt concluded that there is a positive correlation between -ly adverb avoidance and novels’ perceived literary merit.

Which finding, if true, would most clearly be an exception to the pattern Blatt identified?
choices: The novels of Virginia Woolf, one of the most celebrated writers of the twentieth century, have an average of 116 -ly adverbs per 10,000 words, while the novels of Jane Austen, one of the most celebrated writers of the nineteenth century, have an average of 128 -ly adverbs per 10,000 words.

William Faulkner’s classic novel The Sound and the Fury has the lowest -ly adverb rate among Faulkner’s novels in Blatt’s study, while F. Scott Fitzgerald’s classic novel The Great Gatsby has the lowest -ly adverb rate among Fitzgerald’s novels in Blatt’s study.

D.H. Lawrence’s acclaimed novel Women in Love and novels by several genre fiction authors that many critics regard as lacking in artistic quality have a comparable number of -ly adverbs per 10,000 words.

Whereas award-winning and best-selling novels have on average 114 and 115 -ly adverbs per 10,000 words, respectively, fan fiction novels, which are frequently authored by nonprofessional authors, have on average 154 -ly adverbs per 10,000 words.
explanation:
Logic: To be an exception, look for a highly regarded novel with many -ly adverbs or a poorly regarded novel with few -ly adverbs. That would break the positive correlation between avoiding -ly adverbs and literary merit.

A. Incorrect: It compares two acclaimed authors and doesn't contradict the overall pattern.
B. Incorrect: Both classic novels have the lowest adverb rates among their authors' works, supporting the pattern.
C. Correct: An acclaimed novel and low-quality novels having similar adverb rates contradicts the claimed correlation.
D. Incorrect: Fan fiction having more -ly adverbs than acclaimed novels supports the pattern.

question:
In public and political discourse, the implementation of green space in urban planning is generally treated as an obvious strategy for effective local abatement of major air pollutants (such as NO₂, O₃, and particulate matter). <u>Research indicates that the role of such spaces is nuanced, however.</u> Zander S. Venter et al. analyzed data at three spatial scales (street, neighborhood, and city) from 2010 to 2019 at air-quality monitoring stations in Albania, the US state of West Virginia, and thousands of other locations. When coupled with images from aerial surveys of vegetation patterns at those locations in the same time period, the data reveal several factors mediating the relationship between vegetation and air quality.

Which finding from the study by Venter et al., if true, would most directly support the underlined claim?
choices: The association between total green space and pollutant levels is much more variable at the smallest spatial scale than at the largest, and the association is more strongly negative in areas situated in coniferous forest biomes, especially when considering particulate matter.

Regardless of total green space, locations with policies targeting the reduction of anthropogenic emissions have experienced larger improvements in air quality than locations with policies targeting the abatement of emitted pollutants have.

The effect size of total green space on ambient air quality remained consistent by location despite localized deviations from typical weather patterns, such as heat waves, that are known to cause spikes in ambient air pollution.
There is a moderately positive association between total green space and air quality across all locations, and the association persists even when the data are disaggregated by spatial scale.
explanation:
Logic: The claim says green space has a nuanced relationship with air quality, so the best evidence should show that the relationship varies depending on conditions rather than remaining constant.

A. Correct: It shows the relationship changes by spatial scale, biome, and pollutant type.
B. Incorrect: It focuses on emissions policies rather than green space.
C. Incorrect: A consistent effect suggests the relationship is simple, not nuanced.
D. Incorrect: A uniformly positive relationship also contradicts the idea of nuance.

question:
Exclusively inhabiting tropical countries such as Cameroon, wild chimpanzees lack adaptations to seasonal variations in ultraviolet B (UVB) irradiance from sunlight; since UVB exposure enables vertebrates to synthesize vitamin D, Sophie Moittié and colleagues studied zoo chimpanzees in Norway and other mid-latitude countries to see how vitamin D levels are affected by the seasonal variations in UVB irradiance that occur in those locations. They found that chimpanzees’ vitamin D levels were significantly lower in winter than in summer and appeared unaffected by oral supplementation of vitamin D administered by zookeepers. Moittié and colleagues point out, however, that supplementation was rare, highly varied, and poorly tracked, and therefore _______

Which choice most logically completes the text?
choices: differences in vitamin D supplementation likely explain more of the difference in vitamin D levels across zoo chimpanzees in Norway and other mid-latitude countries than seasonal differences in UVB irradiation do.
the possibility that zoo chimpanzees in Norway and other mid-latitude countries would benefit from supplemental vitamin D during winter cannot be excluded.
vitamin D levels in zoo chimpanzees in Norway and other mid-latitude countries may be higher during winter than Moittié and colleagues’ data appear to indicate.
the effect of supplemental vitamin D on zoo chimpanzees in Norway and other mid-latitude countries can more clearly be observed in summer than in winter.
explanation:
Logic: Because vitamin D supplementation was rare and poorly tracked, the researchers cannot conclude that supplementation is ineffective.

A. Incorrect: The study found seasonal UVB differences, not supplementation, best explained vitamin D levels.
B. Correct: Poor supplementation data mean its potential benefits cannot be ruled out.
C. Incorrect: The data themselves are not questioned.
D. Incorrect: The study provides no evidence that supplementation works better in summer.

question:
Because scholars have yet to decipher the script of the Olmec civilization—which flourished in southern Mexico circa 1500 BCE–400 BCE—they are uncertain which language the Olmecs spoke. However, the ancient Olmec sites are situated in the territory of the Mixe-Zoquean family, a group of related languages that includes such present-day representatives as Totontepec Mixe and Rayón Zoque. Moreover, many words in the region’s contemporary Mayan languages—languages otherwise unrelated to the Mixe-Zoquean family—are Mixe-Zoquean in origin. Such lexical borrowing may have occurred because a Mixe-Zoquean language served as a medium of cultural exchange throughout southern Mexico during the era of Olmec hegemony, which would suggest that _______

Which choice most logically completes the text?
choices: the language of the Olmec civilization likely belonged to the same language family as Totontepec Mixe and Rayón Zoque.
the languages of the Mixe-Zoquean and Maya peoples alike may derive from a precursor language spoken in the region before the rise of the Olmec civilization.
speakers of Mayan languages likely used Totontepec Mixe and Rayón Zoque as mediums of cultural exchange even after the decline of the Olmec civilization.
the Olmecs may have spoken a language that was closer to Mayan languages than to Mixe-Zoquean languages.
explanation:
Logic: If a Mixe-Zoquean language served as the region's language of cultural exchange during Olmec rule, that supports the idea that the Olmecs themselves likely spoke a Mixe-Zoquean language.

A. Correct: This follows logically from the linguistic evidence presented.
B. Incorrect: The passage doesn't suggest a common ancestral language.
C. Incorrect: Totontepec Mixe and Rayón Zoque are modern languages, not the historical lingua franca.
D. Incorrect: The evidence points toward Mixe-Zoquean, not Mayan.

question:
During the Bronze Age, collections of metal objects (called hoards) were buried for safekeeping all over Britain. Earlier discoveries of these hoards, such as the discovery around 1931 of the Towednack hoard (which included gold jewelry from the 10th century BCE), were rare and often accidental. But since the 1960s, advancements such as inexpensive metal detectors, ground-penetrating radar, and aerial surveys have made it much easier to locate hoards while they are still underground. A more recent find like the 2011 discovery of the Boughton Malherbe hoard was thus much more likely than a pre-1960s discovery to _______

Which choice most logically completes the text?
choices: include rare items from the 10th century BCE.
result from artifacts being unearthed accidentally.
occur before the ground was disturbed.
explanation:
Logic: Modern technology allows archaeologists to detect hoards before digging disturbs the site, unlike many earlier accidental discoveries.

A. Incorrect: Modern technology doesn't make gold jewelry more likely.
B. Incorrect: The age of the artifacts is unrelated.
C. Incorrect: Pre-1960 discoveries were more likely to be accidental.
D. Correct: Ground-penetrating radar and aerial surveys allow hoards to be found before excavation.

question:
Enacted in 1953, Denmark’s 6,221-word constitution, in contrast to Chile’s, which was enacted in 1980 and contains a far greater number (25,821) of words, _______ as the 13th shortest in the world. Such data are studied by constitutional scholars like George Tsebelis, who can use them to draw broader conclusions.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation:
Logic: The subject is Denmark's constitution, which is singular, so it needs a singular present-tense verb.

A. Correct: Ranks agrees with the singular subject.
B. Incorrect: The progressive tense is unnecessary.
C. Incorrect: Rank is plural.
D. Incorrect: The present perfect doesn't fit the sentence.

question:
Many folktales that originate in the Hindi language start with a phrase that roughly translates to “it’s an old story.” Many tales that originate in English use “once upon a time.” Such phrases, known as story starters, _______ from language to language.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation:
Logic: The subject is Such phrases, which is plural, so it requires the plural verb vary.

A. Incorrect: Is varying is singular and unnecessarily progressive.
B. Correct: Vary agrees with the plural subject.
C. Incorrect: Has varied is singular.
D. Incorrect: Varies is singular.

question:
Ford Madox Ford’s classic novel about two couples living in Europe was first published in 1915. Of the many revisions that Ford made before publication, the change to the book’s title is among the most ______ Ford had originally called the novel The Saddest Story, but he ultimately published it as The Good Soldier—a title that shifted the focus to the novel’s strongly ironic tone.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation:
Logic: The second clause explains which revision was noteworthy, so a colon correctly introduces that explanation.

A. Correct: The colon properly introduces the explanation.
B. Incorrect: No punctuation creates a run-on.
C. Incorrect: A comma cannot join two independent clauses.
D. Incorrect: An em dash is less appropriate because the second clause directly explains the first.

question:
While improvising, a guitarist may add expression without causing dissonance by swapping the V chord for its opposite, the iv chord. This concept of harmonic opposites originated in the music theory text A Theory of Harmony (1985) by Ernst Levy. British musician Jacob Collier ______ Levy’s concept and, in a 2017 YouTube interview that went viral among music theory enthusiasts, give it the name “negative harmony.”

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation:
Logic: The passage narrates past events in chronological order, so the simple past tense is needed.

A. Correct: Would popularize ...and (would) give... works

B. Incorrect: Had popularized ...and (had) give... does not work

C. Incorrect: Popularized ...and give... does not work

D. Incorrect: Has popularized ...and (has) give... does not work

question:
As categorized by linguists like Isidore Dyen, the languages Cebuano and Malagasy—spoken by roughly 30 million and 17 million people, ______ are part of the Austronesian language family, which altogether accounts for one-fifth of the world’s languages.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation:
Logic: The phrase "spoken by roughly 30 million and 17 million people, respectively," is parenthetical information. Since the sentence continues after it, the parenthetical should be closed with a comma.

A. Incorrect: It fails to separate the parenthetical phrase from the main clause.
B. Incorrect: An em dash is unnecessary because the phrase is not being specially emphasized.
C. Correct: The comma correctly closes the parenthetical before the main clause continues.
D. Incorrect: A colon cannot separate a parenthetical phrase from the main clause.

question:
In a US presidential election, Massachusetts’s 11 electoral votes are currently awarded to the winner of Massachusetts’s popular vote, but a new plan aims to change that. Law professors Akhil and Vikram Amar’s 2001 article ______ that states could instead agree to allocate their electoral votes to the winner of the national popular vote has given rise to the National Popular Vote Interstate Compact (NPVIC).

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation:
Logic: The sentence's main verb is "has given rise." The blank should therefore contain a participial phrase modifying "article."

A. Correct: Suggesting correctly modifies "article."
B. Incorrect: Suggested creates two main verbs.
C. Incorrect: Has suggested also creates two finite verbs.
D. Incorrect: Suggests creates another main verb.

question:
Oats, olives, and many other species of plants were brought to the Western Hemisphere after the late 15th century. These species were native to the continents of ______ Africa, and Asia in the Eastern Hemisphere.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation:
Logic: The sentence lists three continents in a simple series, so commas should separate the items.

A. Incorrect: The list items are not properly separated.
B. Correct: The comma correctly separates Europe, Africa, and Asia.
C. Incorrect: A semicolon is unnecessary in a simple list.
D. Incorrect: A colon cannot separate items within a series.

question:
Oats, olives, and many other species of plants were brought to the Western Hemisphere after the late 15th century. These species were native to the continents of ______ blank Africa, and Asia in the Eastern Hemisphere.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

The early Australian railroad system of the 1800s was famously uncoordinated. Trains on the narrow gauge Mackay Railway line in Queensland couldn't travel on the Yarra Valley Railway in Victoria, which used broad gauge tracks, without performing time-consuming conversions. ______ historians refer to this complicated system as the “mixed gauge muddle.”

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
explanation:
Logic: The inability to travel between rail systems is the reason historians call the network the "mixed gauge muddle." The relationship is cause and effect.

A. Incorrect: The second sentence is not expressing similarity.
B. Correct: Hence shows that the nickname follows from the described problem.
C. Incorrect: There is no contrast.
D. Incorrect: The second sentence is not another example.

question:
The Duchy of Gaeta, a sea power based in the Mediterranean port city of Gaeta that reached its height around 900 CE, is considered a thalassocracy—a geopolitical entity whose hegemony resulted from control of the sea rather than of land. Historians classify thalassocracies as distinct from tellurocracies, or land-based powers. ______ the British Empire (1600s–1900s CE) is known for both land and sea supremacy.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
choices: For example, tellurocracies have long overpowered their rivals:
Of course, the distinction is not always so neat:
In other words, empires are classified according to their source of power:
explanation:
Logic: The British Empire controlled both land and sea, making it an exception to the neat distinction between thalassocracies and tellurocracies.

A. Incorrect: The sentence is not giving an example of tellurocracies overpowering rivals.
B. Correct: It introduces an exception to the previous distinction.
C. Incorrect: It merely repeats the definition of a thalassocracy.
D. Incorrect: The British Empire doesn't simply restate the classification system.

question:
The Sino-Tibetan language of Kurtöp has only about 15,000 living speakers. Although most Kurtöp speakers live in Bhutan, where the language originated, Kurtöp is also spoken in New York City. ______ the New York–based Endangered Language Alliance has identified a group of Kurtöp speakers in the city's Sunnyside neighborhood, in the borough of Queens.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
explanation:
Logic: The final sentence gives a specific example of the statement that Kurtöp is spoken in New York City.

A. Correct: Specifically introduces the supporting example.
B. Incorrect: The sentences are not occurring simultaneously.
C. Incorrect: The second sentence doesn't simply add another unrelated fact.
D. Incorrect: There is no contrast.

question:
Seventeenth-century baroque artist Pietro da Cortona famously created a trompe l'oeil—an illusion of three-dimensional space on a two-dimensional surface—in the interior of the Palazzo Barberini in Rome, Italy. In actuality, the frescoed ceiling of the palace is mostly flat. Da Cortona's artful use of forced perspective, ______ creates the illusion of dozens of allegorical figures rising into the sky.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
explanation:
Logic: The third sentence restates and explains how the illusion is created after noting that the ceiling is actually flat.

A. Incorrect: The flat ceiling doesn't cause the illusion.
B. Incorrect: The sentence isn't introducing a new example.
C. Incorrect: It explains rather than contrasts.
D. Correct: In other words signals a restatement of the trompe l'oeil effect.

question:

question:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:

• In music theory, the term “key” refers to the set of musical notes that forms the foundation of a piece of music.
• In Règles de Composition (1682), French composer Marc-Antoine Charpentier describes the moods of various musical keys.
• He describes the key of E minor as “amorous.”
• In On the Sensations of Tone (1863), German physicist Hermann von Helmholtz undertakes the same task.
• He describes the key of E minor as “restlessness.”
• “Eleanor Rigby” by the Beatles (1966) is a song written in E minor.
The student wants to compare how Charpentier and Helmholtz describe the mood of E minor. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
choices: The song “Eleanor Rigby” by the Beatles is written in the key of E minor, the mood of which has been described as “amorous.”
The key of E minor is one of various keys, which are sets of musical notes that form the foundations of pieces of music.
Charpentier describes the mood of E minor as “amorous,” while Helmholtz describes it as “restlessness.”
Charpentier and Helmholtz each undertook the task of describing the mood of various keys, including E minor.
explanation:
Logic: The goal is to compare how Charpentier and Helmholtz described the mood of E minor, so the answer should state both descriptions.

A. Incorrect: It mentions only Charpentier's description.
B. Incorrect: It defines a musical key rather than comparing the two composers.
C. Correct: It directly compares Charpentier's "amorous" with Helmholtz's "restlessness."
D. Incorrect: It notes that both described keys but doesn't compare their descriptions of E minor.

question:
The following text is from Jhumpa Lahiri’s 2003 novel The Namesake. Gogol, a child, is at a beach in Massachusetts with his father.

On the beach Gogol collects rocks, digs tunnels in the sand. He and his father <u>wander</u> barefoot, their pant legs rolled halfway up their calves. He watches his father raise a kite within minutes into the wind, so high that Gogol must tip his head back in order to see, a rippling speck against the sky.

As used in the text, what does the word “wander” most nearly mean?
explanation:
Don’t use the first definition you know. Replace “wander” with each answer choice and see which one fits the sentence: “He and his father ___ barefoot…”

Correct answer: C. Walk
“Wander” here means to walk around casually without a specific destination. Gogol and his father are moving around barefoot on the beach.

Incorrect answers:
A. Vary — “wander” can sometimes mean “deviate” or “vary,” but people do not “vary barefoot” on a beach.
B. Compete — nothing in the sentence suggests a contest or competition.
D. Increase — “wander” does not mean grow larger or increase in this context.

question:
The fact that publications by University of Chicago economist Nancy L. Stokey, who studies economic growth and development, are so frequently cited in other scholars’ work ______ the usefulness of her research for her peers—other economists clearly find her studies valuable for their own scholarship.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
explanation:
The clue is: “other economists clearly find her studies valuable.” Frequent citations are evidence that her research is useful.

Correct answer: B. testifies to
“Testifies to” means gives evidence of or shows. The fact that Stokey’s publications are frequently cited shows the usefulness of her research.

Incorrect answers:
A. conflicts with — this means contradicts. Frequent citations do not contradict the usefulness of her research; they support it.
C. distracts from — citations do not take attention away from her research’s usefulness.
D. fluctuates with — this means changes together with, but the sentence is not about something rising and falling over time.

question:
The following text is from Charles Dickens’s 1861 novel Great Expectations. The narrator is taking a walk near his home on a damp morning.

On every rail and gate, wet lay clammy, and the marsh mist was so thick, that the wooden finger on the post directing people to our village—a direction which they never <u>accepted</u>, for they never came there—was invisible to me until I was quite close under it.

As used in the text, what does the word “accepted” most nearly mean?
explanation:
The key phrase is “the wooden finger on the post directing people to our village.” The “direction” means the route/sign pointing people toward the village. So “accepted” means people did or did not take/follow that direction.

Correct answer: A. Followed
“Accepted” here means followed. The sign points people toward the village, but they “never accepted” that direction because they never came there.

Incorrect answers:
B. Allowed — “allowed a direction” does not fit the idea of a sign pointing the way.
C. Modified — nothing suggests people changed or adjusted the direction.
D. Approved — “accepted” can sometimes mean approved, but here it is about whether people followed the sign’s direction, not whether they agreed with it.

It indicates that an explanation offered by Bilkovic and Roggero has been replaced by a more plausible one.

Los Angeles–Long Beach–Anaheim | 5,979,000 | 45.1% | 393,051 | 26.5%

Percent Change in Average Global Market Prices by Commodity in Two Agricultural Trade-Reform Scenarios

Commodity | Percent change in TFA scenario | Percent change in tariff-removal scenario
Coarse grains (excluding rice, wheat, and maize) | −1.35 | +0.81
Milk products | −1.48 | −0.30
Oilseeds | −1.67 | +1.26
Sugar | −0.74 | +0.37

Ratified in 2017 by two-thirds of World Trade Organization member nations, the Trade Facilitation Agreement (TFA) is a trade-reform measure that aims to reduce import and export fees and other costly aspects of international trade. In a 2021 report, economist Jayson Beckman modeled global market prices of several agricultural commodities under both the TFA and an alternative trade-reform scenario: removal of agricultural tariffs (taxes on imports that generally increase prices on imported goods). After reviewing data from the report, a student concludes that overall, consumers of the commodities listed in the table would likely benefit more from the TFA than they would from tariff removal.

Which choice most effectively uses data from the table to support the student’s claim?
choices: Under the tariff-removal scenario, the average price of milk products would increase, but the average prices of coarse grains and sugar would decrease.
Under the TFA scenario, the average prices of all four commodities would decrease, whereas under the tariff-removal scenario, only the average price of milk products would decrease.

Under the TFA scenario, the average price of sugar would decrease by a smaller amount than any of the other three commodities’ prices would, whereas its average price would increase under the tariff-removal scenario.
Under the tariff-removal scenario, the average prices of milk products, coarse grains, and oilseeds would decrease by more than 1%, while the average price of sugar would decrease by less than 1%.
explanation:
B supports the last statement because the last statement says consumers would benefit more from the TFA than from tariff removal.

Consumers benefit when prices go down because they can buy goods for less.

Choice B says:

Under the TFA scenario, prices for all four commodities decrease.

But under the tariff-removal scenario, only milk products decrease.

So B directly proves that TFA is better for consumers overall: TFA lowers more prices, while tariff removal mostly raises prices.

question:
Average Frequencies of LP Allele in Four European Regions

Region* | Iron Age | Modern-day
Germany | 7% | 48%
Great Britain | 50% | 73%
Hungary | 7% | 48%
Portugal | 9% | 40%

*Referred to by the names of corresponding present-day nations

Relatively high average levels of lactase persistence (LP)—which preserves the ability to digest lactose, or milk sugar, into adulthood—have typically been found in past and present populations in which milk, cheese, and other dairy products are a major source of nutrition after infancy. Using genetic data from archaeological sites in Great Britain (such as Amesbury) and across continental Europe, David Reich, Ali Akbari, and colleagues studied average frequencies during Europe’s Iron Age (700–1 BCE) of the allele that confers this trait in Europeans. The researchers concluded that during that period, dairy products were likely a more important part of people’s diet in what is today Great Britain than they were in other parts of Europe.

Which choice best describes data from the table that support the researchers’ conclusion?
choices: The reported average frequency of the LP allele is 73% for Great Britain during the Iron Age, whereas the highest reported average frequency in any of the other European countries shown is 48%.
For each region, the reported average frequency of the LP allele is notably higher for modern times than it is for the Iron Age.
The reported average frequency of the LP allele during the Iron Age is much higher for Great Britain than it is for other parts of Europe.
The reported average frequency of the LP allele during the Iron Age in Great Britain is 50%.
explanation:
The researchers’ conclusion is about the Iron Age: dairy was likely more important in Great Britain than in other parts of Europe.

The table shows:

Great Britain, Iron Age: 50%
Germany, Iron Age: 7%
Hungary, Iron Age: 7%
Portugal, Iron Age: 9%

So Great Britain’s Iron Age LP allele frequency was much higher than the others. Since LP is connected to digesting milk into adulthood, this supports the idea that dairy was more important in Great Britain during that time.

Why not D?
D is true, but it only says Great Britain was 50%. It doesn’t compare Great Britain to the other regions, so it doesn’t fully support the conclusion.

question:
Andrea Sommese, Ákos Pogány, and team investigated head-tilting behavior in a group of forty dogs, which included thirty-four typical dogs from five different breeds (including Enzo, a whippet) and six dogs that had previously demonstrated giftedness at learning words, all of which were border collies. The researchers recorded the dogs’ head-tilting behavior in response to requests to fetch a toy that had been introduced early in the study. They found that all six gifted dogs tilted their heads at least some of the time when asked to retrieve the toy by name, while the typical dogs almost never tilted their heads. After reviewing the study, a student concludes that a tendency to tilt their heads is a characteristic trait of all border collies.

Which finding from the study, if true, would most directly challenge the student’s conclusion?
choices: The typical dogs that tilted their heads appeared to be processing the meaning of the requests.
Most of the gifted dogs tilted their heads to the same side in each trial.
The majority of dogs in the typical group were border collies
The border collies successfully fetched the toy more often than the dogs of other breeds did.
explanation:
Logic.
State the passage claim as a testable prediction before comparing the choices. The needed evidence must show that the majority of dogs in the typical group were border collies. This result directly strengthens the claim while the other choices do not test it.

Correct answer. C.
C. This choice is correct because the finding that the majority of dogs in the typical group were border collies directly supports the claim that a tendency to tilt their heads is a characteristic trait of all border collies.

Incorrect answers.
A. This choice is incorrect because the statement that the typical dogs that tilted their heads appeared to be processing the meaning of the requests does not provide the evidence required by the passage.
B. This choice is incorrect because the statement that most of the gifted dogs tilted their heads to the same side in each trial does not provide the evidence required by the passage.
D. This choice is incorrect because the statement that the border collies successfully fetched the toy more often than the dogs of other breeds did does not provide the evidence required by the passage.

question:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:

• Extravehicular activities (EVAs) are activities performed outside a spacecraft by astronauts in outer space.
• EVAs are also known as spacewalks.
• Jerry Ross is a former US astronaut who has performed 9 spacewalks.
• The total time of Ross’s spacewalks was 58 hours and 32 minutes.
• Benjamin Alvin Drew is a former US astronaut who has performed 2 spacewalks.
• The total time of Drew’s spacewalks was 12 hours and 48 minutes.
The student wants to emphasize a similarity between the astronauts Ross and Drew. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
choices: Drew has spent less time performing spacewalks than Ross has.
Ross and Drew have each performed multiple spacewalks.
EVAs, also known as spacewalks, are activities done by astronauts outside a spacecraft.
Ross has performed spacewalks, but Drew has performed EVAs.
explanation:
B is correct.

The goal is to emphasize a similarity between Ross and Drew.

Choice B says:

Ross and Drew have each performed multiple spacewalks.

That shows what they have in common: both astronauts performed more than one spacewalk.

Why A is wrong:
A says Drew spent less time spacewalking than Ross. That emphasizes a difference, not a similarity.

Why C is wrong:
C defines EVAs/spacewalks, but it doesn’t compare Ross and Drew.

Why D is wrong:
EVAs and spacewalks mean the same thing, but the sentence uses “but,” which makes it sound like a contrast. It’s not the clearest way to show similarity.

question:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:

• Calida Garcia Rawles is an African American painter.
• She is known for her large-scale, hyperrealistic paintings depicting African American figures in water.
• The painting Lost in the Shuffle (36 × 24 in) depicts two young men with their arms outstretched floating in the bottom left and upper right corners of the canvas.
• Guardian (96 × 48 in) depicts a woman in a white dress floating in the center of the canvas.
• She paints the water with vivid blue colors, including sapphire blue and ultramarine.
• The mood in the paintings is serene.
Which choice most effectively uses information from the given sentences to emphasize a difference between the two paintings?
choices: Among the many stunning works of Calida Garcia Rawles is Guardian, a serene 96-by-48-inch painting depicting a woman floating in a white dress in the vivid blue water.
Although the number of figures may differ, constant among Rawles’s hyperrealistic works is the serene mood that the paintings evoke.
Calida Garcia Rawles captures the water in paintings such as Lost in the Shuffle and Guardian in vivid hues of sapphire blue and ultramarine.
While some of Rawles’s works, such as Lost in the Shuffle, feature two figures in the composition, Guardian features one figure floating in the vivid blue water.
explanation:
The goal is to emphasize a difference between the two paintings.

Choice D does that clearly:

Lost in the Shuffle features two figures, while Guardian features one figure.

That is a direct difference between the two paintings.

Why A is not best:
A only describes Guardian. It does not compare Guardian to Lost in the Shuffle, so it does not emphasize a difference between the two paintings.

Why B is not best:
B starts with a difference, but then focuses on a similarity: both paintings have a serene mood.

Why C is not best:
C emphasizes a similarity: both paintings use vivid blue water colors.

So the answer should be D.

question:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:

• The Geocenter in Copenhagen, Denmark, is home to a Foucault pendulum.
• The pendulum consists of a weighted ball that swings at the end of a roughly 25-meter-long cable.
• Like all Foucault pendulums, it dangles from a fixed point that ensures the swing path of the pendulum doesn’t change.
• To an observer, the swing path of a Foucault pendulum appears to change over time because Earth rotates beneath it.
• Foucault pendulums are used as a simple way to provide evidence of Earth’s rotation.
The student wants to specify the parts of a Foucault pendulum. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
choices: With a swing path that appears to change over time, a Foucault pendulum provides evidence of Earth’s rotation.
The swing path of the Foucault pendulum at the Geocenter appears to change over time.
The Foucault pendulum at the Geocenter in Copenhagen, Denmark, includes a cable that is roughly 25 meters long.
Dangling from a fixed point, the Foucault pendulum at the Geocenter consists of a cable with a weighted ball at the end.
explanation:
The goal is to specify the parts of a Foucault pendulum.

Choice D names the actual parts:

fixed point
cable
weighted ball

So it directly answers what the pendulum is made of:

“Dangling from a fixed point, the Foucault pendulum at the Geocenter consists of a cable with a weighted ball at the end.”

Why the others are wrong:

A explains the purpose/evidence of a Foucault pendulum, not its parts.

B describes the swing path, not the parts.

C gives only one part — the cable — so it is incomplete.

So the best answer is D.

question:

question:

question:
In a 2024 study, Kliebenstein and colleagues examined whether the composition of soil microbial communities could affect plants’ flavor chemistry. Whereas Baslam et al. (2011) showed that adding specific bacterial or fungal strains to soil can yield increased flavonoid content in spinach crops, Kliebenstein and team applied intact microbial communities gathered from ecologically distinct settings across Colorado, including areas of sagebrush and irrigated pasture, to mustard plants and evaluated the flavor compounds in the plants’ seeds. This ensured that the microbial conditions in their experiment would better reflect the variation and complexity of naturally occurring communities.

Based on the text, what is the most likely reason Kliebenstein and colleagues chose to avoid the method used in the spinach study?
choices: The microbial community in the soil from the spinach study affected plants’ nutrition, not their flavor chemistry.
The diversity of species of microorganisms in the soil from the spinach study was already abnormally high before the researchers added further microorganisms.
The composition of microorganisms in the soil in the spinach study may not have been representative of a naturally existing composition.

question:
"The Monster” is an 1898 story by Stephen Crane. In the story, the character of Jimmie is a young boy who has been scolded by his father for accidentally damaging a flower in his garden; Jimmie then looks for sympathy from Henry Johnson, the man responsible for the care of Jimmie’s father’s horses. Crane demonstrates Henry’s tendency towards such sympathy, writing, _____

Which quotation from “The Monster” most effectively illustrates the claim?
choices: “Henry would sometimes choose to absolutely repudiate [Jimmie’s behavior], and when Jimmie appeared in his shame would bully him most virtuously, preaching with assurance the precepts of [Jimmie’s father’s] creed, and pointing out to Jimmie all of his abominations.”

“Henry... could usually provide a sin to place himself on a footing with the disgraced one. Perhaps he would remember that he had forgotten to put the hitching-strap in the back of the buggy on some recent occasion, and had been reprimanded by [Jimmie’s father].”
“Henry personally conducted [Jimmie’s father] during the splendid journeys through the country roads, where farms spread on all sides, with sheep, cows, and other marvels abounding.”
“In regard to almost everything in life [Jimmie and Henry] seemed to have minds precisely alike.”
explanation:
The claim we need to prove is that Henry tends to show sympathy toward Jimmie when Jimmie is in trouble.

B works because Henry “could usually provide a sin” of his own, meaning he remembers something bad he also did so he can be on the same level as Jimmie. Instead of judging Jimmie, Henry makes Jimmie feel less alone by showing, “I’ve messed up too.” That is sympathy.

Why the others are wrong:

A says Henry sometimes rejects Jimmie’s behavior and lectures him. That shows criticism, not sympathy.

C is just about Henry driving Jimmie’s father through the country. It doesn’t show Henry comforting Jimmie.

D says Jimmie and Henry thought alike about many things. That shows similarity, but it doesn’t specifically show Henry being sympathetic when Jimmie is ashamed.

question:
Describing adverbs “as damaging to a writer,” novelist Graham Greene is one of several authors and literary critics to recommend minimizing the use of adverbs, especially those ending in -ly (e.g., “diligently”), in works of fiction. To investigate the prevalence of -ly adverbs in novels, Ben Blatt used natural language processing—machine learning technology that reads and interprets text—to calculate the rates at which these words occur in both popular fiction and in novels that commonly appear on lists of notable works of English literature, such as Theodore Dreiser’s Sister Carrie. Blatt concluded that there is a positive correlation between -ly adverb avoidance and novels’ perceived literary merit.

Which finding, if true, would most clearly be an exception to the pattern Blatt identified?
choices: The novels of Virginia Woolf, one of the most celebrated writers of the twentieth century, have an average of 116 -ly adverbs per 10,000 words, while the novels of Jane Austen, one of the most celebrated writers of the nineteenth century, have an average of 128 -ly adverbs per 10,000 words.

Whereas award-winning and best-selling novels have on average 114 and 115 -ly adverbs per 10,000 words, respectively, fan fiction novels, which are frequently authored by nonprofessional authors, have on average 154 -ly adverbs per 10,000 words.

D.H. Lawrence’s acclaimed novel Women in Love and novels by several genre fiction authors that many critics regard as lacking in artistic quality have a comparable number of -ly adverbs per 10,000 words.

William Faulkner’s classic novel The Sound and the Fury has the lowest -ly adverb rate among Faulkner’s novels in Blatt’s study, while F. Scott Fitzgerald’s classic novel The Great Gatsby has the lowest -ly adverb rate among Fitzgerald’s novels in Blatt’s study.

question:
In public and political discourse, the implementation of green space in urban planning is generally treated as an obvious strategy for effective local abatement of major air pollutants (such as NO₂, O₃, and particulate matter). <u>Research indicates that the role of such spaces is nuanced, however.</u> Zander S. Venter et al. analyzed data at three spatial scales (street, neighborhood, and city) from 2010 to 2019 at air-quality monitoring stations in Germany, the US state of Kentucky, and thousands of other locations. When coupled with images from aerial surveys of vegetation patterns at those locations in the same time period, the data reveal several factors mediating the relationship between vegetation and air quality.

Which finding from the study by Venter et al., if true, would most directly support the underlined claim?
choices: There is a moderately positive association between total green space and air quality across all locations, and the association persists even when the data are disaggregated by spatial scale.

Regardless of total green space, locations with policies targeting the reduction of anthropogenic emissions have experienced larger improvements in air quality than locations with policies targeting the abatement of emitted pollutants have.

The effect size of total green space on ambient air quality remained consistent by location despite localized deviations from typical weather patterns, such as heat waves, that are known to cause spikes in ambient air pollution.

The association between total green space and pollutant levels is much more variable at the smallest spatial scale than at the largest, and the association is more strongly negative in areas situated in coniferous forest biomes, especially when considering particulate matter.
explanation:
The underlined claim says the role of green spaces is nuanced — meaning it is not simple or not always the same.

Choice D supports that because it says the relationship between green space and pollution levels changes depending on several factors:

spatial scale: the effect is more variable at the street/smallest scale than at the largest scale
biome/location type: the effect is stronger in coniferous forest areas
pollutant type: especially when considering particulate matter

So D shows that green space does not have one simple, consistent effect on air quality. Its effect depends on context, which directly supports the idea that the role of green spaces is nuanced.

A is wrong because it makes the relationship sound simple and consistently positive across all locations and scales, which does not support “nuanced.”

question:

choices: differences in vitamin D supplementation likely explain more of the difference in vitamin D levels across zoo chimpanzees in Ireland and other mid-latitude countries than seasonal differences in UVB irradiation do.
the effect of supplemental vitamin D on zoo chimpanzees in Ireland and other mid-latitude countries can more clearly be observed in summer than in winter.
vitamin D levels in zoo chimpanzees in Ireland and other mid-latitude countries may be higher during winter than Moittié and colleagues’ data appear to indicate.
the possibility that zoo chimpanzees in Ireland and other mid-latitude countries would benefit from supplemental vitamin D during winter cannot be excluded.

question:

speakers of Mayan languages likely used Ulterior-Mixe and Francisco León Zoque as mediums of cultural exchange even after the decline of the Olmec civilization.
the language of the Olmec civilization likely belonged to the same language family as Ulterior-Mixe and Francisco León Zoque.
the Olmecs may have spoken a language that was closer to Mayan languages than to Mixe-Zoquean languages.

question:

question:

• He describes the key of A minor as “tender and plaintive.”
• In Ideas Toward an Aesthetic of Music (1806), German poet and composer Christian Schubart undertakes the same task.
• He describes the key of A minor as having “tenderness of character.”
• “Ain’t No Sunshine” by Bill Withers (1971) is a song written in A minor.
The student wants to compare how Charpentier and Schubart describe the mood of A minor. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
choices: Charpentier describes the mood of A minor as “tender and plaintive,” while Schubart describes it as having “tenderness of character.”
Charpentier and Schubart each undertook the task of describing the mood of various keys, including A minor.
The song “Ain’t No Sunshine” by Bill Withers is written in the key of A minor, the mood of which has been described as “tender and plaintive.”
The key of A minor is one of various keys, which are sets of musical notes that form the foundations of pieces of music.
explanation:

The task is very specific: compare how Charpentier and Schubart describe the mood of A minor. So the best answer should mention both people and give both descriptions side by side.

Correct answer: A.
It directly compares the two descriptions:

Charpentier: “tender and plaintive”
Schubart: “tenderness of character”

That is exactly what the question asks for.

D. Just defines key and says A minor is one of them; it doesn’t address the comparison at all.

question:

question:

Information in the text best supports which statement about OFT?
choices: It may be weakened by the finding that the costs and benefits associated with a particular ecological circumstance vary by species.

question:
Optimal foraging theory (OFT) holds that animals’ foraging behaviors reflect cost-benefit trade-offs that vary by species and with dynamic ecological circumstances. One such circumstance is lunar intensity, which Mary V. Price and colleagues found to be negatively associated with foraging by white-throated woodrats but Simon Kenneth Bearder and colleagues found to be positively associated with foraging by Mohol bushbabies. This discrepancy is explicable in terms of OFT: the bushbabies’ greater reliance on vision means that higher lunar intensity benefits them more than it benefits the woodrats.

Information in the text best supports which statement about Mohol bushbabies?
choices: If increased lunar intensity imposed the same costs on the bushbabies that it imposes on white-throated woodrats, there would be no association between lunar intensity and the bushbabies’ foraging.

If the advantages that the bushbabies gain from increased lunar intensity explain the change in their foraging behavior, those advantages are likely shared by some other species that are not heavily reliant on vision.
If increased lunar intensity creates any disadvantages for the bushbabies, those disadvantages are more than compensated for by the advantages that the bushbabies gain.
If the bushbabies’ foraging behavior under increased lunar intensity actually reflects a cost-benefit trade-off, their behavior should be more similar to that of white-throated woodrats than it is.

Which choice most effectively uses data from the graph to complete the example?
